ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r1.claim: Al-Jinn complements Sūrah Nūḥ: the prior sūrah showed Noah’s leaders rejecting their messenger, while this one shows the Qur’an moving jinn to spread its message among their kin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r1.anchor: This sūrah is the counterpart of S ūrah N ūḥ the previous sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r2.claim: The jinn’s encounter is also alluded to in al-Aḥqāf; it is recounted to awaken Quraysh’s honor, since non-addressee jinn were moved while Quraysh turned against the Qur’an and its messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r2.anchor: if the jinn, who are not even the direct addressees of the Qur’ ān could be so deeply moved

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r3.claim: The account reassures the Prophet not to grieve over Quraysh’s rejection: dead hearts will not benefit, but even accidental listeners with some capacity for truth can.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r3.anchor: those who even have the slightest ability to appreciate the truth will benefit from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r4.claim: The passage addresses Quraysh idolaters, who believed in jinn and maintained a system of soothsaying through contact with them, rather than people who accept only what the senses detect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p505/r4.anchor: they had also set up a whole system of soothsaying through which they maintained contacts with them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r1.claim: The Qur’an contrasts soothsayers’ reports from mischievous jinn with this report about righteous jinn, offering Quraysh facts about the unseen that can guide those who discern good from evil.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r1.anchor: The Qur’ān has presented before them a report of the righteous among them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r2.claim: Truth-seekers can benefit from these unseen facts; although sense-bound skeptics dismiss them as imagination, providence does not withhold its blessings because some fail to value them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p506/r2.anchor: providence does not deprive people of its blessings if some unworthy elements fail to recognize and value it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r1.claim: The command “tell them” shows that God revealed the jinn’s impressions to the Prophet; they did not narrate them to him directly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r1.anchor: not narrated to the Prophet (sws) directly from their tongue

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r2.claim: A group of jinn happened upon the Prophet while he recited the Qur’an, listened intently, and were moved to call their own people to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r2.anchor: They were so moved by it that they intently listened to what was being recited

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r3.claim: The date is uncertain; the author considers this a detailed account of the incident briefly mentioned in al-Aḥqāf and previously discussed its context through reports.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r3.anchor: In my opinion, this is a detailed version of the same incident referred to

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r4.claim: God has the Prophet convey the report to Quraysh: the Qur’an they disdain deeply affected perceptive jinn, although they were not its direct addressees.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r4.anchor: the same Qur’ ān which they are treating in such a disdainful manner

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r5.claim: “Tell them” is meant to awaken Quraysh’s honor and, in passing, to reassure the Prophet that rejection reflects the rejecters’ evil nature, not a flaw in the Book or messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r5.anchor: it is because of their own evil nature

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r6.claim: The jinn’s announcement was more than praise: recognizing truth and wishing their people well naturally required sharing the divine blessing they had received.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r6.anchor: they did not merely praise the words they heard

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r7.claim: The verbal noun ʿajab is more emphatic than ʿajīb; it describes the Qur’an’s efficacy, force, wisdom, and beauty, rather than something merely strange.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p508/r7.anchor: In Arabic, this word does not mean “strange”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p509/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p509/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p509/r1.claim: The report implies that jinn know both their own language and the local human language, and that some are connoisseurs of that language.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p509/r1.anchor: the jinn are not only conversant with their own language

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r1.claim: They read أوحي in the quadriliteral form; Ibn Abi Abla, al-Ataki from Abu Amr, and Abu Anas al-Asadi read the triliteral form, with the same meaning, supported by al-Ajjaj's poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قل أوحي رباعيا وابن أبي عبلة والعتكي، عن أبي عمرو، وأبو أناس جوية بن عائذ الأسدي: وحى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي وجوية وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r2.claim: They also read أحى by replacing initial waw with hamza; al-Zamakhshari generalizes this as permissible, but Abu Hayyan says the rules differ by a waw's position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وجوية، فيما روي عن الكسائي وابن أبي عبلة أيضا: أحى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r3.speaker: المازني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says al-Mazani allowed the same replacement for waw with kasra, but Abu Hayyan calls this boastful overextension and reports that al-Mazani had both an analogical and a restricted-to-attested view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r3.anchor: وعن المازني في ذلك قولان: أحدهما: القياس كما قال، والآخر: قصر ذلك على السماع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r4.claim: The passive construction means that the hearing of a group of jinn occurred; the common account links it to 46:29 as one event, while another makes the Meccan and Nakhlah encounters two events.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r4.anchor: وأنه استمع في موضع المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله أي استماع نفر من الجن، والمشهور أن هذا الاستماع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r5.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r5.claim: He says the jinn heard the opening revelation, اقرأ باسم ربك; another view says they heard Surat al-Rahman.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r6.claim: A hadith account distinguishes two encounters: first without Ibn Mas'ud near Hira, and a later recitation at al-Hajun with Ibn Mas'ud present and a boundary drawn for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p292/r6.anchor: ويظهر من الحديث «أن ذلك كان مرتين: إحداهما: في مبدأ مبعث رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p304/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p304/r4.speaker: مكحول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p304/r4.claim: Makḥūl says the passage was revealed only concerning the jinn; among them some followed the Prophet on the Night of the Jinn, and seventy thousand were said to have done so before dawn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p304/r4.anchor: قال مكحول: لم ينزل هذا إلا في الجن، أسلم منهم من وفق وكفر من خذل كالإنس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r1.claim: The surah's purpose is to show the Prophet's honor: God softened the hearts of humans, jinn, and others toward him, his companions, and his household, through the Quran's extraordinary character.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r1.anchor: مقصودها إظهار الشرف لهذا النبي الكريم الفاتح صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r2.claim: The Prophet's time among his people was less than a tenth of Noah's, though Noah's people had largely rejected him; the surah's names, al-Jinn and Qul Uhiya, point to its subject.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#s072/r2.anchor: والزمان في آخره وزمان لبثه في قومه دون ربع العشر من زمن نوح

STUDYQURAN:72:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:intro/r1.claim: The late Makkan surah takes its name from the jinn in verse 1 and the report that they heard the Quran, recognized revelation, and embraced Islam.
STUDYQURAN:72:intro/r1.anchor: a group of jinn who heard the Prophet’s recitation of the Quran, recognized it as Divine Revelation, and embraced Islam

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r1.claim: Elmalılı says nefer can denote even one person, while its more familiar Arabic use is for three to ten.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r1.anchor: Bir tek kişiye de “nefer” deriz, Arapça’da ise meşhuru üçten ona kadardır.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r2.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r2.claim: Alusi says eloquent usage also applies nefer to numbers above ten.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r2.anchor: Âlûsî’nin beyânına göre fasihte ondan yukarıya ıtlak olunur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r3.claim: Nefer is not restricted to males or humans, since the verse applies it to jinn too.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r3.anchor: Erlere, hatta inse de mahsus değildir. Çünkü burada cine de ıtlak olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r4.speaker: Mücmel
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r4.claim: Mujmal says reht and nefer can refer to groups up to forty; reht share an ancestor, while nefer do not.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r4.anchor: Mücmel’de demiştir ki: “Reht” ve “nefer” kırka kadar kullanılır, aralarında fark:

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r5.claim: Nefer can also mean a people or group, as in the verse about possessing a larger following.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r5.anchor: “nefer” kavme de ıtlak olunur ki وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًۭا [el-Kehf 18/34] kavl-i celîli bundandır.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r6.speaker: İmâm Kirmânî
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r6.claim: Kirmani gives nefer the customary lexical sense of a man and says a sound hadith was interpreted with that meaning.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r6.anchor: İmâm Kirmânî de “nefer”in örf-i lügatta diğer bir mânası vardır “recül (er)” demiş ve bir hadîs-i sahîhin bu mâna ile tefsir olunduğunu söylemiştir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r7.claim: Elmalılı infers that the local use of nefer derives from its sense of a man.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r7.anchor: Demek ki bizde “nefer” bu mânadan gelmiştir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r8.claim: All readings pronounce anna in the nominative-opening form because the clause is the grammatical subject of uhiya; its attached clauses follow suit, and the pronoun is one of status.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r8.anchor: Bu اَنَّ kıraatlerin hepsinde bi’l-ittifâk üstün okunur. Çünkü cümle أُوحِىَ’nin nâib-i fâili mevkiindedir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r9.claim: Inna is kasra because it introduces the jinn’s quoted speech, and its coordinated clauses likewise take kasra.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r9.anchor: Bu اِنَّا mekūl-i kavl olduğundan bütün kıraatlerde esre okunur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:16/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:16/r1.claim: Exegetes connect verses 16–17 to the opening command “Say,” rather than treating them as the jinn’s speech.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:16/r1.anchor: Müfessirler bu âyetlerin cinlerin sözü değil, sûrenin 1. âyetinin başında yer alan, “De ki ...” buyruğu ile bağlantılı olduğunu kabul ederler

TABATABAI:72:1-17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r1.claim: Asked by Alqama who accompanied the Prophet on the night of the jinn, Ibn Mas'ud says no one did; after searching for the missing Prophet, they met him returning from Hira, and he said a jinn caller took him to recite Qur'an to them and show their traces and fires.
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r1.anchor: قال ما كان منا معه أحد فقدناه ذات ليلة ونحن بمكة فقلنا اغتيل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:72:1-17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r4.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r4.claim: In a report in al-Ihtijaj, jinn meet the Prophet in the valley of date palms, apologize for thinking no messenger would be raised, and seventy-one thousand pledge prayer, fasting, alms, pilgrimage, jihad, and counsel to Muslims.
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r4.anchor: ولقد أقبل إليه أحد وسبعون ألفا منهم فبايعوه على الصوم والصلاة والزكاه والحج والجهاد ونصح المسلمين

TABATABAI:72:1-17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r5.claim: Their pledge matches their statements that they believed and accepted guidance, but how they practiced alms and jihad is unknown, and their first apology remains obscure.
TABATABAI:72:1-17/r5.anchor: يصدقها قولهم المحكي في أول السورة { فآمنا به } وقولهم { وأنا لما سمعنا الهدى آمنا به }

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.claim: People have long disagreed over whether jinn exist: most philosophers apparently deny them, while most religious communities and many ancient philosophers affirm them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.anchor: اختلف الناس قديما وحديثا في ثبوت الجن ونفيه ، فالنقل الظاهر عن أكثر الفلاسفة إنكاره

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.speaker: ابن سينا
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.claim: Ibn Sīnā defines jinn as an airy animal able to assume different forms; Rāzī reads his calling this a definition of the name as evidence he is explaining a term, not affirming an external entity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.anchor: لأن أبا علي بن سينا قال في رسالته في حدود الأشياء الجن حيوان هوائي متشكل بأشكال مختلفة ، ثم قال : وهذا شرح للاسم

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.speaker: أصحاب الروحانيات
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.claim: Many ancient philosophers and spiritualists affirm jinn and call them lower spirits; they say these respond faster but are weaker than celestial spirits, which respond more slowly but are stronger.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.anchor: وزعموا أن الأرواح السفلية أسرع إجابة إلا أنها أضعف ، وأما الأرواح الفلكية فهي أبطأ إجابة إلا أنها أقوى

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.speaker: بعض المثبتين
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.claim: One group of those affirming jinn says they are independent substances, neither bodies nor states inhering in bodies; sharing a negation does not make them equal to God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.anchor: فمنهم من زعم أنها ليست أجساما ولا حالة في الأجسام بل هي جواهر قائمة بأنفسها

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.speaker: بعض المثبتين
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.claim: These proponents say the immaterial beings differ in essence and moral kind: some are good or noble, others evil or base, and only God knows their kinds and number.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.anchor: قالوا : ثم إن هذه الذوات بعد اشتراكها في هذا السلب أنواع مختلفة بالماهية كاختلاف ماهيات الأعراض بعد استوائها في الحاجة إلى المحل

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.speaker: بعض المثبتين
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.claim: They maintain that immaterial jinn can know reported events, hear, see, and perform particular deeds; some kinds can perform feats beyond human power.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.anchor: وكونها موجودات مجردة لا يمنع من كونها عالمة بالخبريات

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.speaker: بعض المثبتين
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.claim: The proponents analogize jinn attachment to bodies with the human soul’s attachment through fine vaporous spirits formed from the blood’s finest parts in the left side of the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.anchor: وكما أنه دلت الدلائل الطبية على أن المتعلق الأول للنفس الناطقة التي ليس الإنسان إلا هي ، هي الأرواح وهي أجسام بخارية لطيفة

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.speaker: بعض المثبتين
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.claim: On this account, a jinn first attaches to a portion of air, then gains influence over a dense body as that air passes through it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.anchor: لم يبعد أيضا أن يكون لكل واحد من هؤلاء الجن تعلق بجزء من أجزاء الهواء ، فيكون ذلك الجزء من الهواء هو المتعلق الأول لذلك الروح

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.claim: Another proposal identifies jinn with departed human souls, which gain strength and insight after death and may attach to a new, similar body to assist its soul.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.anchor: ومن الناس من ذكر في الجن طريقة أخرى فقال : هذه الأرواح البشرية والنفوس الناطقة إذا فارقت أبدانها وازدادت قوة وكمالا

RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.claim: This proposal calls the helper an angel and its influence inspiration when the soul is good, but a devil and whispering when it is evil.
RAZI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.anchor: فإن اتفقت هذه الحالة في النفوس الخيرة سمي ذلك المعين ملكا وتلك الإعانة إلهاما ، وإن اتفقت في النفوس الشريرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r1.speaker: القائلون بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r1.claim: The second broad view says jinn are bodies; its proponents divide over whether bodies themselves differ in their complete essences.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r1.anchor: والقول الثاني : في الجن أنهم أجسام ثم القائلون بهذا المذهب اختلفوا على قولين

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r2.speaker: بعض القائلين بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r2.claim: One bodily view says bodies differ in their essences and share only accidental features: occupying space and having direction and three dimensions.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r2.anchor: منهم من زعم أن الأجسام مختلفة في ماهياتها ، إنما المشترك بينها صفة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r3.speaker: بعض القائلين بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r3.claim: They answer that sharing a single boundary or reality as body does not prove identical essences, just as each accident has one reality without all accidents sharing an essence.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r3.anchor: أما الحجة الأولى : فلأنا نقول ، كما أن الجسم من حيث إنه جسم له حد واحد ، وحقيقة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r4.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r4.claim: The argument invokes philosophers’ claim that accidents have no common essential genus: otherwise the nine categories would be species of one genus, not the highest genera.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r4.anchor: بل الحق عند الفلاسفة أنه ليس للأعراض ألبتة قدر مشترك بينها من الذاتيات

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r5.speaker: بعض القائلين بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r5.claim: By analogy, bodies could differ entirely in essence while sharing only accidental sensible location, spatial occupancy, and dimensions.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r5.anchor: فكذا من الجائز أن تكون ماهيات الأجسام مختلفة في تمام ماهياتها ثم إنها تكون متساوية في وصف عارض

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r6.speaker: بعض القائلين بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r6.claim: A second objection says the division of bodies into subtle and dense, celestial and terrestrial, presupposes one shared bodily reality.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r6.anchor: وأيضا فلأنه يمكننا تقسيم الجسم إلى اللطيف والكثيف ، والعلوي والسفلي

RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r7.speaker: بعض القائلين بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v30p132/r7.claim: These proponents call both objections weak: divided things may share an accidental property while differing in essence, as bodies might share location and dimensions.

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.claim: Dividing bodies into subtle and dense does not prove that all bodies share a common essence, just as dividing accidents into quality and quantity does not establish shared essential properties.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.anchor: يمكن تقسيم العرض إلى الكيف والكم ولم يلزم أن يكون هناك قدر مشترك من الذاتي

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.claim: A subtle airy body could differ essentially from other air, with its nature entailing distinctive knowledge and extraordinary power; this makes jinn and their ability to assume forms plausible.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.anchor: لا يمتنع في بعض الأجسام اللطيفة الهوائية أن تكون مخالفة لسائر أنواع الهواء في الماهية

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.speaker: الأشعري وجمهور أتباعه
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.claim: Al-Ashʿarī and most followers deny that bodily structure is a condition for life.

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.claim: Their argument is that one life cannot inhere simultaneously in many substrates; if each equal part had its own life, dependence between the parts would create a circle, so an individual part can live independently.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.anchor: والأول محال لأن حلول العرض الواحد في المحال الكثيرة دفعة واحدة غير معقول

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that structure is necessary because life disappears when the structure breaks down and remains while it stays intact.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.anchor: وأما دليل المعتزلة وهو أنه لا بد من البنية فليس إلا الاستقراء

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.claim: Rāzī rejects that induction as proof of necessity: observed cases do not establish the state of unobserved cases, and the inference assumes that miracles cannot break ordinary patterns.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.anchor: فإن الاستقراء لا يفيد القطع بالوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.claim: Since life need not depend on structure, God can give an individual atom knowledge and power for difficult acts, making jinn possible whether their bodies are subtle or dense and their parts large or small.
RAZI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.anchor: أن يخلق الله تعالى في الجوهر الفرد علما بأمور كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r1.speaker: الأشعري
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r1.claim: Al-Ashʿarī permits a present visible object to go unperceived even when the sense is sound, conditions are met, and obstacles are absent; the Muʿtazilites deem this rationally impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r1.anchor: أما الأشعري وأتباعه فقد جوزوه ، وأما المعتزلة فقد حكموا بامتناعه عقلا

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r2.claim: The distant large object appears small because only some of its parts are seen, though the perceptual conditions apply equally to unseen parts; perception is therefore not necessary when conditions obtain.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r2.anchor: أنا نرى الكبير من البعد صغيرا وما ذاك إلا أنا نرى بعض أجزاء ذلك البعيد دون البعض

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r3.claim: If seeing one part depends on seeing another, equal parts produce circular dependence; if not, an atom could be seen alone, though an isolated atom is not seen, showing perception is possible rather than necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r3.anchor: فإما أن تكون رؤية هذا الجزء مشروطة برؤية ذلك الجزء الآخر أو لا تكون

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites object that allowing nonperception under adequate conditions would mean nearby drums and horns might not be seen or heard.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r4.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد عولوا على أنا لو جوزنا ذلك لجوزنا أن يكون بحضرتنا طبلات وبوقات

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r5.claim: Rāzī says this objection leaves no principled distinction between regular habits and necessities: the same reasoning would permit seas turning to gold, mountains to jewels, or extra suns appearing unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r5.anchor: والسبب في هذا التشوش أن هؤلاء المعتزلة نظروا إلى هذه الأمور المطردة في مناهج العادات

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r6.claim: He says one must treat all such events alike, either as necessary as the philosophers do or as nonnecessary as al-Ashʿarī does; an arbitrary split is untenable.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r6.anchor: بل الواجب أن يسوى بين الكل

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r7.claim: On al-Ashʿarī’s account, jinn may be powerful, dense bodies yet remain unseen even while present.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r7.anchor: فإن أجسامهم وإن كانت كثيفة قوية إلا أنه يمتنع أن لا تراها

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r8.claim: The Qurʾān says angels and jinn can perform difficult acts, which would require dense, solid organs on the Muʿtazilite premise; angels attend people, the Prophet, and the dying without being seen.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r8.anchor: على أن للملائكة قوة عظيمة على الأفعال الشاقة

RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r9.claim: If powerful angels and jinn are subtle, that contradicts the claim that subtle bodies cannot do hard work; if they are dense, their frequent presence without being seen contradicts the Muʿtazilite view of perception.
RAZI-FULL:v30p133/r9.anchor: وإن قالوا : إنها أجسام لطيفة وحية ، ولكنها للطافتها لا تقدر

RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet did not see the jinn: after heaven was guarded and meteors drove them away, investigators reached Tihāma, heard the Prophet reciting at dawn in ʿUkāẓ, recognized the cause, and returned to warn their people.
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r1.anchor: وهو مذهب ابن عباس أنه عليه السلام ما رآهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās infers that the Prophet had not seen them because, had he witnessed the event, he would not have attributed his knowledge of it to revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r2.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أنه عليه السلام لم ير الجن إذ لو رآهم لما أسند معرفة هذه الواقعة إلى الوحي

RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r3.claim: One reconciliation is that jinn were accompanying the devils when the latter were struck by meteors while spying on heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r3.anchor: فيه وجهان الأول : أن الجن كانوا مع الشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r4.claim: Alternatively, the ones struck by meteors were themselves jinn, called devils because a shayṭān is any rebellious being far from obedience to God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r4.anchor: الثاني : أن الذين رموا بالشهب كانوا من الجن

RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r5.speaker: عاصم عن ذر
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r5.claim: A report from ʿĀṣim via Dharr identifies the visitors as a group led by Zawbaʿa and his companions, who heard the Prophet recite in Mecca and returned; Rāzī links this to 46:29.
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r5.anchor: روى عاصم عن ذر قال : قدم رهط زوبعة وأصحابه

RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r6.claim: Another view identifies them as the Shayṣabān, the most numerous jinn and the main body of Iblīs’s troops.
RAZI-FULL:v30p134/r6.anchor: وقيل : كانوا من الشيصبان وهم أكثر الجن عددا

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Prophet was ordered to go to the jinn and recite the Qurʾān; he accompanied him to al-Ḥajūn, where a throng of jinn gathered, heard the recitation, and remained unseen to him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r1.anchor: وهو مذهب ابن مسعود أنه أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمسير إليهم ليقرأ القرآن عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r2.claim: In another version, the jinn ask who the Prophet is and for a witness; a tree comes, testifies that he is God’s Messenger, then returns to its place.
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r2.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى فقالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما أنت

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r3.claim: The jinn later ask for provisions, and the Prophet gives them bones and dung; he forbids people to use either as food.

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r4.claim: Rāzī says the reports about Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd cannot be rejected and offers several ways to reconcile them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r4.anchor: واعلم أنه لا سبيل إلى تكذيب الروايات

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r5.claim: The event Ibn ʿAbbās describes may have happened first, with revelation of this sūra, followed later by the Prophet’s instructed visit described by Ibn Masʿūd.
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r5.anchor: لعل ما ذكره ابن عباس وقع أولا

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r6.claim: If there was one event, the Prophet may have visited and recited without knowing what the jinn said or did, and God then revealed it to him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r6.anchor: إلا أنه عليه السلام ما عرف أنهم ماذا قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r7.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet saw and heard the believing jinn; after they returned and told their people what had happened, God revealed their account to him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p135/r7.anchor: وهو عليه السلام رآهم وسمع كلامهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r1.claim: The command “Say” tells the Prophet to disclose to his companions what God revealed about the jinn episode; Rāzī lists its benefits: the Prophet’s mission includes jinn, Quraysh see the Qurʾān’s inimitability, jinn are morally responsible, understand human speech, and believing jinn call their kin to faith.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r1.anchor: وفيه فوائد إحداها : أن يعرفوا بذلك أنه عليه السلام كما بعث إلى الإنس

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r2.claim: Wahy is the discreet casting of meaning into the soul, as inspiration or an angel’s descent, and is done rapidly.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r2.anchor: الإيحاء إلقاء المعنى إلى النفس في خفاء كالإلهام وإنزال الملك

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r3.speaker: يونس وهرون عن أبي عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r3.claim: The common reading is awḥā with an alif; Yūnus and Hārūn report that Abū ʿAmr read waḥā with ḍamma on wāw and no alif.

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r4.speaker: قُرِىء
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r4.claim: Another reading is aḥyā, with hamza instead of the original wāw, by analogy with aʿada and azana.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r4.anchor: وقرىء { * أحي } بالهمز من غير واو

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r5.claim: They agree that anna in “that a group of jinn listened” takes fatḥ because the clause is the passive subject of awḥā; Rāzī compares 6:19.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r5.anchor: أجمعوا على أن قوله : { أنه استمع } بالفتح

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r6.claim: They agree on kasr for innā in “we heard,” since it begins a quoted independent clause after the verb of saying.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r6.anchor: وأجمعوا على كسر إنا في قوله : { إنا سمعنا } لأنه مبتدأ محكي بعد القول

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.claim: One reading pattern gives fatḥ to clauses that belong to revelation and kasr to the jinn’s speech; the final clauses about mosques and the Prophet’s standing are exceptions to the jinn’s speech.

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r8.claim: A second pattern opens all the following clauses by supplying “we believed in it and believed that…,” including the claims about the Lord’s greatness and the fool’s speech.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r8.anchor: وثانيهما : فتح الكل والتقدير : فآمنا به وآمنا بأنه تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r9.claim: This second parsing faces two objections: attaching belief to clauses such as “our fool used to say” sounds improper, and Arabic does not coordinate onto a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r9.anchor: أحدهما : أنه يقبح إضافة الإيمان إلى بعض هذه السورة

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r10.claim: Rāzī answers that taking āmannā to mean “we affirmed and testified” resolves both objections.
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r10.anchor: والجواب : عن الإشكالين أنا إذا حملنا قوله : آمنا على معنى صدقنا

STUDYQURAN:72:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r1.claim: The jinn listened to the Prophet reciting the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r1.anchor: The jinn listened to the Prophet’s recitation of the Quran (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:72:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r2.claim: After returning, the jinn are said to have addressed their own community, marveling at and affirming the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r2.anchor: to their own community of jinn upon their return (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:72:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r3.claim: This event is also identified with the jinn encounter in 46:29–32.
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r3.anchor: This event is also said to be the one referred to in 46:29–32

STUDYQURAN:72:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r4.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r4.claim: “A wondrous Quran” can mean “an amazing Quran,” whose unparalleled eloquence amazed the jinn as it did human beings.
STUDYQURAN:72:1/r4.anchor: which is understood as a reference to an unparalleled eloquence that amazed the jinn (Bg)

TABATABAI:72:1-2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r1.claim: The Meccan sūra recounts jinn who heard the Qurʾan and believed its foundational teachings, then records the Prophet’s mission, God’s oneness in lordship, and resurrection.
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r1.anchor: تشير السورة إلى قصة نفر من الجن استمعوا القرآن فآمنوا به وأقروا بأصول معارفه

TABATABAI:72:1-2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r2.claim: The Prophet is ordered to tell his people the story; God is the revealer, and the object of ‘listened’—the Qurʾan—is omitted because the wording makes it clear.
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r2.anchor: أمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يقص القصة لقومه، والموحي هو الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:72:1-2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r3.speaker: المشهور
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r3.claim: The commonly cited range for nafar is a group of three to nine.
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r3.anchor: والنفر الجماعة من ثلاثة إلى تسعة على المشهور

TABATABAI:72:1-2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r4.claim: An alternative reported range for nafar is up to forty people.

TABATABAI:72:1-2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r5.claim: ʿAjab is what prompts wonder by departing from the ordinary; the jinn call the Qurʾan wondrous because its wording and meaning are extraordinary and an unlettered man who could neither read nor write brought it.
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r5.anchor: والعجب بفتحتين ما يدعو إلى التعجب منه لخروجه عن العادة الجارية في مثله

TABATABAI:72:1-2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r7.claim: The jinn returned to their people and reported hearing extraordinary recited speech that guides to true knowledge and deeds, bringing genuine felicity.
TABATABAI:72:1-2/r7.anchor: فقالوا - لقومهم لما رجعوا إليهم - إنا سمعنا كلاما مقروا خارقا للعادة

TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r1.claim: Jinn and humans were created to worship God; the author cites this as evidence of the jinn’s religious obligation.
TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r1.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس الا ليعبدون

TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r2.claim: The jinn report that they heard a wondrous Qurʾan, were guided to rightness, and believed it; they include believers.
TABATABAI:72:1-2#2/r2.anchor: إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا * يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r1.claim: Sura al-Jinn is Makkan and consists of twenty-eight verses.

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r2.claim: The command is addressed to Muhammad, telling him to convey this to his people.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r2.anchor: يا محمد لقومك {أوحى إلى} أي ألقى على بطريق الوحي

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r3.claim: Waḥy means a hidden communication or report from God; disclosing this news shows Muhammad is messenger to both jinn and humankind, forbids shirk, and urges tawhid.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r3.anchor: ألقى على بطريق الوحي وأخبرت بأعلام من الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r4.claim: The opening أنَّه is accusative as the subject of أوحي, and its pronoun refers to the matter or affair being reported.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r4.anchor: بالفتح لأنه فاعل أوحى والضمير الشأن أي أن الشأن والحديث

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r5.claim: The object of استمع is omitted and may be Qur'an, Ṭā Hā, or اقرأ, understood from what follows.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r5.anchor: أي القرآن أو طه أو اقرأ وقد حذف لدلالة ما بعده عليه

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r6.claim: An attentive listener intentionally listens; a hearer may catch sound without intending to, so every listener hears but not every hearer listens.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r6.anchor: والمستمع من كان قاصدا للسماع مصغيا إليه والسامع من اتفق سماعه من غير قصد إليه

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r7.claim: Nafar means a group of jinn numbering more than three but fewer than ten.

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r8.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r8.claim: Al-Qamus defines nafar as fewer than ten men and gives anfār as its plural.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r8.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : النفر ما دون العشرة من الرجال كالنفير

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that at Fajr in Nakhlah, while Muhammad and companions prayed after traveling toward Ukaz, passing jinn heard the Quran and listened; the Prophet neither saw nor knew them, nor had recited to them deliberately, and learned of them by revelation.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما انطلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه إلى سوق عكاظ

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r10.claim: Jinn are subtle bodies in forms unlike angels and humans, ordinarily hidden from human sight; they can address miracle workers and whisper to other people.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r10.anchor: والجن أجسام رقاق فيصورة تخالف صورة الملك

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r11.claim: Jinn are predominantly fiery or airy; the author cites the Quran's creation of jinn from a smokeless flame and explains beings by whichever of the four elements predominates.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r11.anchor: يغلب عليهم النارية أو الهوائية ويدل على الأول مثل قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r12.claim: Most philosophers deny that jinn exist externally, while many ancient philosophers and most religious communities affirm their existence.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r12.anchor: وأكثر الفلاسفة ينكرون وجود الجن في الخارج واعترف به جمع عظيم من قدمائهم وكذا جمهور أرباب الملل

BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r13.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r13.claim: Al-Qashani describes jinn as earthly souls less dense than animal natures yet unlike human or pure spiritual souls, attached to subtle airy, fiery, or smoky elemental forms called suspended images by some philosophers.
BURSEVI:v10p144#3/r13.anchor: قال القاشاني : إن في الوجود نفوسا أرضية قوية لا في غلظ التقوس السبعية والبهيمة

BURSEVI:v10p145/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p145/r1.claim: Al-Qashani says jinn have cognitions like ours and, being near the heavenly realm, can receive some unseen knowledge and ascend to overhear angels, understood as disembodied souls.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r1.anchor: أمكنها أن تتلقى من عالمه بعض الغيب فلا يستبعد أن ترتقى أفق السماء فتسترق السمع من كلام الملائكة

BURSEVI:v10p145/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r2.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p145/r2.claim: Despite their earthly weakness, heavenly forces repel them from higher knowledge; smoky bodies may ignite under stars' rays and perish or be driven back down, possibilities confirmed by truthful prophets and saints.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r2.anchor: ولما كان أرضية ضعيفة بالنسبة إلى القوى السماوية تأثرت تلك القوى فرجمت بتأثيرها عن بلوغ شأوها

BURSEVI:v10p145/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r3.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p145/r3.claim: Al-Qashani locates jinn within human existence too, concealed in the unseen inward realm.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r3.anchor: وهي في الوجود الإنساني لاستتارها في غيب الباطن

BURSEVI:v10p145/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p145/r4.claim: The jinn spoke these words to their own people when they returned to them.

BURSEVI:v10p145/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p145/r5.claim: They call it a Quran because it is a book recited on the Messenger's tongue.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r5.anchor: قرءانا} أي كتابا مقروأ على لسان الرسول

BURSEVI:v10p145/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p145/r6.claim: The verbal noun عجَب is used adjectivally for emphasis; the Quran is wondrous because it exceeds familiar likenesses and human speech in arrangement and subtle meaning.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r6.anchor: مصدر بمعنى العجيب وضع موضعه للمبالغة والعجيب ما خرج

BURSEVI:v10p145/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r7.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v10p145/r7.claim: Al-Baqli calls it a wondrous, astonishing book and infers that the jinn were people of eloquent language.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r7.anchor: وقال البقلي كتابا عجيبا تكربه وفيه إشارة إلى أنهم كانوا من أهل اللسان

BURSEVI:v10p145/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p145/r8.speaker: عيزار بن حريث
BURSEVI:v10p145/r8.claim: At Ibn Masud's gathering, a traveler related that he and companions buried a wounded snake; two jinn women later identified it as Amr, the last of those who heard the Prophet's Quran, killed in fighting between believing and unbelieving jinn. They offered compensation, but the men had acted without seeking worldly return; they praised them. The snake-wrapper was Safwan ibn Muattal al-Muradi.
BURSEVI:v10p145/r8.anchor: قال عيزارين حريث كنت عند عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه فأتاه رجل فقال له كنا في سفر

TABRISI:72:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:72:1/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the opening annahu with fatḥ; he also uses fatḥ in the listed clauses through the jinn’s affirmations, with kasr in the other clauses except istiqāmū and al-masājid.
TABRISI:72:1/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر { قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع } بفتح الألف

TABRISI:72:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1/r2.speaker: الرواة عن أبي جعفر
TABRISI:72:1/r2.claim: His transmitters say clauses referred to revelation take fatḥ and the jinn’s own speech takes kasr, but this rule does not fit his reported reading; transmission may contain an error.
TABRISI:72:1/r2.anchor: قال الرواة عنه ما كان مردودا على الوحي فهو أنه بالفتح وما كان من قول الجن فهو بالكسر

TABRISI:72:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1/r6.speaker: جوية بن عابد
TABRISI:72:1/r6.claim: A rare reading attributed to Juwayya ibn ʿĀbid has qil aḥyi ilayya.
TABRISI:72:1/r6.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة جوية بن عابد قل أحي إلي

TABRISI:72:1-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-10/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-10/r2.claim: The rare form aḥyi comes from waḥaytu ilayhi, meaning awḥaytu; initial wāw becomes hamza after obligatory ḍamma, as in uqit for wuqqit.
TABRISI:72:1-10/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ أحي فهو من وحيت إليه بمعنى أوحيت وأصله وحي

TABRISI:72:1-10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-10/r3.speaker: العجاج
TABRISI:72:1-10/r3.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s verse uses waḥā as a witness for the root form.
TABRISI:72:1-10/r3.anchor: قال العجاج: وحى لها القرار فاستقرت

TABRISI:72:1-2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-2/r2.claim: God commands Muhammad to tell his people what they did not know; the passive “it was revealed” magnifies the revelation, which God sent through an angel.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r2.anchor: إنما ذكره على لفظ ما لم يسم فاعله تفخيما وتعظيما والله سبحانه أوحى إليه

TABRISI:72:1-2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-2/r3.claim: Jinn are light-bodied beings in a distinctive form, unlike humans made of clay and angels made of light; jinn are made of fire.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r3.anchor: وهم جيل رقاق الأجسام خفيفة على صورة مخصوصة بخلاف صورة الإنسان والملائكة

TABRISI:72:1-2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-2/r4.claim: “They said” means that some of the jinn spoke to the others.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r4.anchor: فقالوا } أي قالت الجن بعضها لبعض

TABRISI:72:1-2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-2/r5.claim: The Qur’an is wondrous because its distinctive composition exceeds ordinary speech, its cause is hidden, and it differs from human speech in meaning, eloquence, and form; none can match it.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r5.anchor: فلما كان القرآن قد خرج بتأليفه المخصوص عن العادة في الكلام وخفي سببه

TABRISI:72:1-2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-2/r6.claim: Its wonder also lies in recounting past and future events through an unlettered man among an unlettered people.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r6.anchor: وقد تضمن أخبار الأولين والآخرين وما كان وما يكون أجراه الله على يد رجل أمي

TABRISI:72:1-2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-2/r9.claim: The passage shows Muhammad was sent to jinn and humans, and that jinn are rational, accountable, know Arabic, recognize miracles, and invited their people to Islam and the Qur’an’s inimitability.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r9.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان مبعوثا إلى الجن والإنس وعلى أن الجن عقلاء مخاطبون

TABRISI:72:1-2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:72:1-2/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas through Saʿid ibn Jubayr that the Prophet neither recited to nor saw the jinn: after being barred from heavenly news, a group heard his dawn recitation at Nakhlah near ʿUkāẓ and returned to their people. Bukhari and Muslim also report it in their Ṣaḥīḥs.
TABRISI:72:1-2/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن

THALABI:v10p49#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p49#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p49#3/r1.claim: The jinn who listened were nine from Nasibin, and they heard the Prophet reciting; their story was already related.
THALABI:v10p49#3/r1.anchor: وكانوا تسعة من جن نصيبين استمعوا قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v10p49#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p49#3/r2.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
THALABI:v10p49#3/r2.claim: Abu Hamza al-Thumali says they belonged to the Banu al-Shaytan, the most numerous jinn and the main body of Iblis's troops.
THALABI:v10p49#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو حمزة الثمالي: بلغنا أنهم من بني الشيطان وهم أكثر الجن عددا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that while the Prophet prayed and recited at night, a group of jinn listened, drew close in love of the Quran, nearly climbed over him, believed, and returned to their people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r1.anchor: يصلي من الليل، ويقرأ القرآن، مر به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi refers back to his account of why the jinn came to the Prophet at al-Aḥqāf 29.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r2.anchor: الجن إياه عند قوله: {وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن} [الأحقاف: 29]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ʿajaban as eloquent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r3.anchor: وقالوا: {إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا}، يعني: بليغا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r4.claim: Muqatil says it means noble and without equal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {قرآنا عجبا} يعني عزيزا لا يوجد مثله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r5.claim: It is a wondrous Quran that astonishes by its eloquence and unmatched character.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p279#2/r5.anchor: قرآنا ذا عجيب، يعجب منه لبلاغته وعدم مثله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r1.claim: The Prophet was informed by revelation from God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r1.anchor: { قل أوحي إلي } أي: أخبرت بالوحي من الله إلي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r2.claim: God sent a group of jinn to listen to the Prophet reciting the dawn prayer at Batn Nakhlah; they are the group mentioned in Sūrat al-Aḥqāf.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r2.anchor: بعث نفرا من الجن ليستمعوا قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي الصبح ببطن نخلة، وهؤلاء الذين ذكرهم الله في سورة الأحقاف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r3.claim: On returning to their people, the jinn called the Qur’an amazing for its eloquence, clarity, and truthful reports.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:1/r3.anchor: { إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا } في فصاحته وبيانه وصدق إخباره.

QASHANI:72:1-2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:1-2/r1.claim: Jinn are powerful terrestrial souls, intermediate between coarse animal souls, human souls, and subtle disembodied souls, attached to delicate elemental bodies dominated by air, fire, or smoke.
QASHANI:72:1-2/r1.anchor: نفوسا أرضية قوية لا في غلظ النفوس السبعية والبهيمية وكثافتها وقلة إدراكها

QASHANI:72:1-2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r2.speaker: بعض الحكماء
QASHANI:72:1-2/r2.claim: Some philosophers call these beings suspended images; Qashani says they possess forms of knowledge and perception like ours.

QASHANI:72:1-2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:1-2/r3.claim: Their natural nearness to the heavenly realm lets them receive some unseen knowledge and ascend to overhear the angels, who are disembodied souls; celestial powers repel their weaker earthly souls.
QASHANI:72:1-2/r3.anchor: قريبة بالطبع إلى الملكوت السماوية أمكنها أن تتلقى من عالمها بعض الغيب

QASHANI:72:1-2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:1-2/r4.claim: Their smoky bodies may ignite under starlight and perish, or celestial influence may bar them from ascent and send them downward; such events are possible.
QASHANI:72:1-2/r4.anchor: تشتعل أجرامها الدخانية بأشعة الكواكب فتحترق وتهلك أو تنزجر من الارتقاء إلى الأفق السماوي

QASHANI:72:1-2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:1-2/r5.claim: Qashani supports these accounts by appealing to truthful prophets and saints who witnessed them, especially Muhammad.
QASHANI:72:1-2/r5.anchor: وقد أخبر عنها أهل الكشف والعيان الصادقون من الأنبياء والأولياء خصوصا أكملهم نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

QASHANI:72:1-2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:1-2/r6.claim: In the inward application, the heart receives revelation while the inner faculties—imagination, estimation, thought, both intellects, and other perceptions—listen as the human being's jinn.
QASHANI:72:1-2/r6.anchor: القلب إذا استعد لتلقي الوحي وكلام الغيب استمع إليه القوى النفسانية من المتخيلة والوهم والفكر والعاقلة النظرية والعملية وجميع المدركات الباطنة التي هي جن الوجود الإنساني

QASHANI:72:1-2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:1-2/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:1-2/r7.claim: Divine speech brought through the Holy Spirit differs from crafted speech of imagination or conclusions of rational syllogisms; its light revives the faculties and guides them rightly.
QASHANI:72:1-2/r7.anchor: لم يكن الكلام الإلهي الوارد على القلب بواسطة روح القدس من جنس الكلام المصنوع المتلقف بالفكر والتخيل أو المستنتج من القياسات العقلية والمقدمات الوهمية والتخيلية

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r1.claim: The word jinn derives from janna, “to conceal,” and means hidden or unseen beings; its singular is jinnī.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r1.anchor: Sözlükte cin, “örtmek, gizli kalmak” anlamındaki cenne fiilinden isim olup “gizli, görünmeyen varlıklar” mânasına gelir, tekili cinnîdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r2.claim: Jinn are created from fire, imperceptible to the senses, conscious and free-willed, accountable to divine commands, and include good and bad beings like humans.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r2.anchor: Terim olarak cin, ateşten yaratılmış, duyularla idrak edilemeyen, şuur ve irade sahibi, ilâhî emirlere uymakla yükümlü olan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r3.claim: The Qur’an uses jinn in 22 places; Islamic sources use it for the third rational, conscious species besides humans and angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r3.anchor: Cin kelimesi gerek Kur’an’da (22 yerde) gerekse diğer İslâmî kaynaklarda insan ve melek dışındaki üçüncü bir akıllı / şuurlu varlık türünün adı olarak kullanılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r4.claim: Jinn marry and reproduce, have greater power than humans, can travel far quickly, see people unseen, and know some things humans do not, but cannot know the unseen.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r4.anchor: İnsanlar gibi cinler de kendi aralarında evlenip çoğalırlar; insanlara nisbetle daha üstün bir güce sahiptirler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r5.claim: Jinn cannot secretly obtain reports from angels’ conversations in heaven.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r5.anchor: Gökteki meleklerin konuşmalarından gizlice haber almak isterlerse de buna imkân verilmez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r6.claim: Some jinn served in Solomon’s army and worked alongside humans.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r6.anchor: Kur’an bazı cinlerin Hz. Süleyman’ın emrine girerek ordusunda hizmet gördüklerini ve insanlarla beraber çalıştıklarını bildirmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r7.claim: Historical beliefs varied: Assyrians and Babylonians feared evil spirits, Semitic peoples posited classes of jinn, Egyptians likened them to reptiles, Greeks divided superhuman daimones into good and evil, and Romans feared harmful spirits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r7.anchor: Eski Asurlular ve Bâbilliler’de kötü ruh ve cinlere inanılırdı. Sâmî kökenli kavimlerde cinlerin değişik sınıfları bulunduğu kabul edilirdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r8.claim: Chinese traditions placed good and evil jinn everywhere, Taoist priests used charms and spells for protection, Indians also accepted good and evil jinn, Iranian beliefs predated Zoroastrianism, and ancient Turks blamed jinn for illness and used shamans to expel them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r8.anchor: Çinliler’de cinlerin her yerde bulunduğu, iyi ve kötülerinin olduğu kabul edilirdi. Özellikle taoist rahipleri cinlerin zararlarından korunmak için muska yazar, efsun yaparlardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r9.claim: Jewish jinn beliefs, sharpened partly by Iranian dualism, placed them in deserts and ruins; Jewish scriptures describe jinn causing pain and calamity and sucking blood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r9.anchor: İsrail kültüründe, daha çok İran’ın düalist sisteminin tesiriyle kötü ruh ve cin anlayışı belirginleşmişti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r10.claim: Christian demon beliefs developed mainly under Jewish influence; the New Testament associates demons with pagan gods and bodily or mental illness, and demon lore later became prominent in Christian art and Western witchcraft.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r10.anchor: Hıristiyan kültüründe cin telakkisi daha çok Yahudilik etkisinde gelişmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r11.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs attributed divine powers to jinn, sacrificed to them, and believed they brought heavenly information to soothsayers, linking them with God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r11.anchor: İslâm’dan önce Araplar cinlere bazı tanrısal güç ve yetenekler yükler, onlar adına kurban keserlerdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r12.claim: Some pre-Islamic Arabs treated Satan as an evil god and jinn as his soldiers, but the Qur’an rejects these beliefs and says jinn, like humans, were created to worship God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r12.anchor: Câhiliye Arapları’nın bir kısmı şeytanın şer tanrısı olduğuna inanır, melekleri Allah’ın askerleri, cinleri de şeytanın askerleri sayarlardı (bk. En‘âm 6/100).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r13.claim: Jinn also received prophets; some believe and others disbelieve, and Muhammad conveyed revelation to them; the commentary also points to the question of jinn’s relations with humans.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r13.anchor: Onlara da peygamber gönderilmiş, içlerinden iman edenler olduğu gibi inkâr edenler de olmuştur (En‘âm 6/130).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r14.claim: A group of jinn heard the Qur’an from the Prophet, believed in its guidance and excellence, and returned to warn their own community against associating anything with God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r14.anchor: cinlerden bir grup, Hz. Peygamber’den Kur’an dinledikten sonra geri dönüp, doğru yolu gösteren ve üstün nitelikleri sebebiyle kendilerini hayran bırakan Kur’an’a inandıklarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r15.claim: The Prophet did not see the jinn listening at that time; revelation informed him, though a later meeting in which he saw and preached to them is reported.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r15.anchor: Hz. Peygamber o esnada Kur’an dinleyen cinleri görmemiş, fakat onların Kur’an dinledikleri kendisine vahiy yoluyla bildirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r16.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r16.claim: The account of jinn hearing the Qur’an is meant to make idolaters, who repeatedly heard it yet persisted in disbelief, learn from the jinn’s example.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:1/r16.anchor: Cinlerin Kur’an’ı dinlediklerini haber vermekten maksat, Hz. Peygamber’den defalarca Kur’an dinledikleri halde iman etmemekte direnen müşriklerin cinlerden ibret ve örnek almalarını sağlamaktır (Şevkânî, V, 350).

BAQILLANI:v1p184/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r1.claim: Recognizing the Qur’an’s inimitability requires learning the proper method and carefully examining its verbal distinctions; otherwise imitation is all one can do. The reader should contemplate with a clear mind and seek God’s help.
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r1.anchor: لكل شيء سبب ولكل علم طريق ولا سبيل إلى الوصول إلى الشيء من غير طريقة ولا بلوغ غايته من غير سبيله خذ الآن هداك الله في تفريغ الفكر

BAQILLANI:v1p184/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r2.claim: Bāqillānī invokes the Qur’an’s descriptions as wise, great, and glorious, and its claims that falsehood cannot reach it, that it humbles a mountain, and that humans and jinn cannot match it.
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r2.anchor: سماه الله عز ذكره حكيما وعظيما ومجيدا

BAQILLANI:v1p184/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r3.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r3.claim: ʿAlī reports that when the Prophet was asked what would save the community from later turmoil, he named God’s mighty Book: seeking guidance elsewhere misleads, while a ruler who judges otherwise is broken by God. The report calls it a clear light, straight path, account of past and future, and a discourse that does not grow stale or exhaust its wonders; the jinn’s response confirms its guidance.
BAQILLANI:v1p184/r3.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال قيل يا رسول الله إن أمتك ستفتتن من بعدك فسأل أو سئل ما المخرج من ذلك فقال بكتاب الله العزيز

BURHAN:v1p273/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.claim: The remaining names include Arabic, connected speech, insight, clarification, knowledge, truth, guidance, wonder, reminder, the firmest bond, similitudes, and truthfulness; Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an is uncreated.
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس غير مخلوق وسماه قولا فقال

BURHAN:v3p256/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p256/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p256/r8.claim: When jinn precede humans, the reason can be chronological: jinn were created earlier, as the explicit wording in the Hijr passage confirms.
BURHAN:v3p256/r8.anchor: وأما تقديم الجن في مواضع أخر

BURHAN:v1p360/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p360/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p360/r1.claim: For the opening إن clauses, a full stop after “do not call anyone with God” suits the kasra reading; with fatḥa, continue through “they almost formed a crowd.”
BURHAN:v1p360/r1.anchor: فإلى قوله ﴿ كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا ﴾

BURHAN:v1p360/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p360/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p360/r2.claim: The fatḥa is best construed as coordinated with the first أن after أوحي, rather than stopping at حطبا and making وأن لو استقاموا an oath.
BURHAN:v1p360/r2.anchor: الأوجه فى ﴿ إن ﴾ فى الآية أن تكون محمولة على ﴿ أوحي ﴾

BURHAN:v1p360/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p360/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p360/r3.claim: Clauses inside the jinn's reported speech cannot be separated by a complete stop from the governing speech, just as a coordinated dependent cannot be cut off from its antecedent.
BURHAN:v1p360/r3.anchor: لأن هذه الجمل داخلة فى القول وما يكون داخلا فى القول لا يتم الوقف دونه كما أن المعطوف إذا تبع المعطوف عليه فى إعرابه

BURHAN:v1p360/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p360/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p360/r4.claim: With both clauses opened, the kasra clauses after إنا سمعنا remain inside the first open أن's predicate, allowing the later open clause to coordinate without an interruption.
BURHAN:v1p360/r4.anchor: فالمكسورات تكون فى خبر المفتوحة الأولى فيعطف عليها الثانية بلا فصل بينها

BURHAN:v1p360/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p360/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p360/r5.claim: He identifies the second open particle with وأن لو استقاموا and the third with وأن المساجد لله.
BURHAN:v1p360/r5.anchor: ثم الثالثة هى التى فى قوله

BURHAN:v1p180/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p180/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p180/r1.claim: The seventh type of sūra opening begins with a command and occurs in six sūras: “Say, it was revealed,” “Read,” and four further “Say” or “I seek refuge” openings.
BURHAN:v1p180/r1.anchor: االسابع الاستفتااح بالأمر فى ست سور

ITQAN:v3p283/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v3p283/r2.claim: Abu Shama counts six sūras that open with a command, including those beginning qul, iqraʾ, and sabbiḥ.
ITQAN:v3p283/r2.anchor: السابع الأمر في ست سور قل أوحي اقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون قل هو الله أحد قل أعوذ المعوذتين

ITQAN:v1p229#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r3.speaker: صاحب المستوفى
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r3.claim: Grammarians dislike an incomplete stop when a complete one is available; in the long jinn passage, stop at 72:18 if the following inna is kasra, but continue to 72:19 if it is fatḥa.
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r3.anchor: قال صاحب المستوفى النحويون يكرهون الوقف الناقص في التنزيل مع إمكان التام

ITQAN:v4p400/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p400/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p400/r5.claim: The jinn group is named as Zawbaʿa, Hasi, Masi, Shasir, Masir, al-Urd, Inyan, al-Ahkam and Saraq.
ITQAN:v4p400/r5.anchor: سمى منهم زوبعة وحسي ومسي وشاصر وماصر

SULAMI:v2p353/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p353/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p353/r1.claim: The jinn marveled at the Quran’s blessings: hearing it gave their hearts spirit, their souls light, their inner selves repose, and their bodies energy to obey its commands.
SULAMI:v2p353/r1.anchor: قال : تعجبت الجن من بركات القرآن لما سمعوه ووجدوا في قلوبهم روحا في أسرارهم نورا

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r1.claim: A surah named by a quoted clause or by a verb with no pronoun is declined like a diptote; an initial wasl hamza is pronounced as a cut hamza in the name.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو حيان في شرح التسهيل ما سمي منها بجملة تحكى نحو ﴿ قل أوحي ﴾ و ﴿ أتى أمر الله ﴾ أو بفعل لا ضمير فيه

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r2.claim: For such names, feminine tāʾ is pronounced hāʾ at pause and written that way because spelling generally follows pause pronunciation.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r2.anchor: إلا ما في أوله همزة وصل فتقطع ألفه وتقلب تاؤه هاء في الوقف ويكتب بهاء على صورة الوقف

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r3.speaker: ابن عصفور
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r3.claim: For a one-letter hijāʾ name followed by “sūrah,” Ibn ʿAsfur treats it as uninflected.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r3.anchor: وما سمي منها باسم فإن كان من حروف الهجاء وهو حرف واحد وأضفت إليه سورة فعند ابن عصفور أنه موقوف لا إعراب فيه

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r4.speaker: الشلوبين
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r4.claim: Al-Shalubin permits an indeclinable form or declension for a one-letter name plus “sūrah,” according to whether it is quoted as a letter or treated as a noun.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r4.anchor: وعند الشلوبين يجوز فيه وجهان الوقف والإعراب أما الأول ويعبر عنه بالحكاية فلأنها حروف مقطعة تحكى كما هي

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r5.claim: A single-letter name without an expressed or understood “sūrah” may be paused on or declined, with inflection depending on its grammatical gender.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r5.anchor: وإن لم تضف إليه سورة لا لفظا ولا تقديرا فلك الوقف والإعراب مصروفا وممنوعا

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r6.claim: Multi-letter names resembling foreign names may be quoted or treated as diptotes, whether or not “sūrah” is added.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r6.anchor: وإن كان أكثر من حرف فإن وزان الأسماء الأعجمية كطاسين وحاميم وأضيفت إليه سورة أم لا فلك الحكاية والإعراب ممنوعا

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r7.claim: A multi-letter name that permits compounding may be quoted, compounded, or declined as a genitive construction, with inflection depending on gender analysis.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r7.anchor: وإن لم يوازن فإن أمكن فيه التركيب كطاسين ميم وأضيفت إليه سورة فلك الحكاية والإعراب إما مركبا مفتوح النون كحضرموت

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r8.speaker: يونس
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r8.claim: Names that cannot be compounded are only quoted or left indeclinable, though Yunus permits declining them as diptotes.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r8.anchor: وإن لم يمكن التركيب فالوقف ليس إلا أضيفت إليه سورة أم لا نحو كهيعص وحمعسق ولا يجوز إعرابه لأنه لا نظير له في الأسماء المعربة

ITQAN:v1p157#3/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r9.claim: A non-letter surah name with the definite article takes genitive; without it, it is normally a diptote unless annexed.
ITQAN:v1p157#3/r9.anchor: وما سمي منها باسم غير حرف الهجاء فإن كان فيه اللام انجر نحو الأنفال والأعراف والأنعام وإلا منع الصرف إن لم يضف إليه سورة

TUSTARI:72:1-2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r1.claim: Nine jinn from Nasibin in Yemen came upon Muhammad reciting in prayer; the term نفر denotes three to ten, and these leading members of their people believed and returned as warners.
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r1.anchor: قال: كان تسعة نفر من نصيبين اليمن، والنفر اسم يقع على الثلاثة إلى العشرة

TUSTARI:72:1-2/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r3.claim: Sahl recounts visiting an ancient city of Aad, where he entered a carved-stone palace and saw a giant in prayer toward the Kaaba, wearing a fresh-looking wool robe.
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r3.anchor: قال سهل: رأيت في دار عاد الأولى مدينة مبنية من حجر، فيها قصر عظيم منقور من حجر يأويه الجن

TUSTARI:72:1-2/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r4.speaker: الجني
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r4.claim: The jinn worshipper says the robe has lasted nine hundred years, during which he met Jesus and Muhammad and believed in them; unlawful food and persistent sins wear out bodies and clothing.
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r4.anchor: فقال: وعليك السلام يا أبا محمد، عجبت لطراوة جبتي وهي علي منذ تسعمائة سنة

TUSTARI:72:1-2/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r5.claim: Sahl reports that Paradise has wild tracts where jinn live, eat, and drink, citing 55:74 as evidence.
TUSTARI:72:1-2/r5.anchor: بلغني أن في الجنة براري يسكنها الجن، ويأكلون فيها ويشربون

KHATTABI:v1p70/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p70/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p70/r1.claim: Umar set out to kill Muhammad, but hearing his sister recite Sūrat Ṭā Hā changed him and he accepted Islam.
KHATTABI:v1p70/r1.anchor: خرج عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - يريد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KHATTABI:v1p70/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p70/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p70/r2.claim: The Quraysh sent ʿUtba to negotiate; after Muhammad recited verses from Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, ʿUtba returned with a changed demeanor.
KHATTABI:v1p70/r2.anchor: أرسلوه بها , فقرأ عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آيات من حم السجدة ,

KHATTABI:v1p70/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p70/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p70/r3.claim: At the pilgrimage season, a group of Anṣār heard the Prophet recite, believed, and carried Islam back to Medina, where they made it public.
KHATTABI:v1p70/r3.anchor: ولما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن في الموسم على النفر الذين حضروه من الأنصار آمنوا به وعادوا إلى المدينة فأظهروا الدين بها

KHATTABI:v1p70/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p70/r4.speaker: بعضهم
KHATTABI:v1p70/r4.claim: A report says the provinces were opened by swords, while Medina was opened by the Qur’an.
KHATTABI:v1p70/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن بعضهم أنه قال: فتحت الأمصار بالسيوف وفتحت المدينة بالقرآن.

KHATTABI:v1p70/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p70/r5.speaker: الجن
KHATTABI:v1p70/r5.claim: The jinn heard the Qur’an and declared it wondrous, guiding to right direction, so they believed in it.
KHATTABI:v1p70/r5.anchor: ولما سمعته الجن لم تتمالك أن قالت: {إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به}

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet neither recited to nor saw the jinn: a group heard his dawn prayer at Nakhla after heavenly news was blocked, then returned to announce wondrous Quran; only their words were revealed to him.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن ولا رآهم ولكنه انطلق في طائفة من أصحابه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r2.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r2.claim: Sahl ibn Abd Allah recounts meeting an enormous jinn in an ancient stone city, praying toward the Kaaba in a wool cloak said to be 700 years old; the jinn attributed decay to sinful smells and unlawful food and claimed faith in Jesus and Muhammad.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p220/r2.anchor: عن سهل بن عبد الله قال كنت في ناحية ديار عاد إذ رأيت مدينة من حجر منقور وسطها قصر

AKHFASH:v2p551/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p551/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p551/r1.claim: The first anna is opened because it is the content of the revelation; he then considers the following clause about the Lord's majesty.
AKHFASH:v2p551/r1.anchor: على الابتداء اذا كان من كلام الجن فان فتح جعله على الوحي وهو حسن

DAMGHANI:v1p314/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r8.claim: ʿAjaban can mean noble or honorable; the jinn describe the Qur'an as noble and distinguished.
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r8.anchor: عجبا اي كريما قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p87/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p87/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p87/r1.claim: Adhān is a call intended to inform the person being called of what is wanted.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p87/r1.anchor: الأذان : نداء يقصد به إعلام المنادى بما يراد منه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r1.claim: Idhn originally means release without restriction; “I gave ear to speech” means that I listened.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r1.anchor: الأصل في الإذن : الإطلاق من غير حجر . وأذنت للحديث استمعت

FARRA:v3p190/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p190/r1.claim: Readers unanimously have passive أوحي; Juwayya al-Asadi reads active أوحى إلي from وحيت, hamzating waw because it is damma-marked, like 81:11.
