FARRA:v3p190/r1.anchor: على (أوحى) وقرأها جوية الأسدى : (قل أوحى إلى) من وحيت

FARRA:v3p190/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p190/r2.claim: After the sky was guarded and devils pelted, Iblis sent nine from Yemen to Mecca; they heard Muhammad reciting at Nakhlah, admired the Quran, and accepted Islam.
FARRA:v3p190/r2.anchor: وبعث تسعة منهم من اليمن إلى مكة، فأتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو ببطن نخلة

FARRA:v3p190/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p190/r3.claim: Readers agree on kasra for إنا here, then differ between kasra and fatḥa on وإنا and أنا through the rest of the sura.
FARRA:v3p190/r3.anchor: وقد اجتمع القراء على كسر «إنا» في قوله: «فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا»

FARRA:v3p190/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r4.speaker: إبراهيم عن علقمة
FARRA:v3p190/r4.claim: Alqama read the later أنا clauses in Jinn and Najm with fatḥa; Yahya, Ibrahim, and Abdullah's companions did likewise.
FARRA:v3p190/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم عن علقمة بن قيس أنه قرأ ما في الجن، والنجم:

FARRA:v3p190/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r5.speaker: نافع والحسن ومجاهد
FARRA:v3p190/r5.claim: Nafiʿ opens; al-Hasan, Mujahid, and most Medinans use kasra, except that they open أن in وأن المساجد لله.
FARRA:v3p190/r5.anchor: وفتح نافع المدني، وكسر الحسن ومجاهد، وأكثر أهل المدينة إلا أنهم نصبوا: «وأن المساجد لله»

FARRA:v3p190/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r7.speaker: عاصم
FARRA:v3p190/r7.claim: Asim reads kasra for jinn speech and fatḥa for clauses spoken as revelation.
FARRA:v3p190/r7.anchor: وكان [عاصم بكسر ما كان] من قول الجن، ويفتح ما كان من الوحي

FARRA:v3p190/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p190/r8.claim: Readers opening all أن clauses link them to فآمنا به as objects of belief; where this sounds awkward, a similar present-tense verb can license fatḥa.
FARRA:v3p190/r8.anchor: ردوا «أن» فى كل السورة على قوله: فآمنا به، وآمنا بكل ذلك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p489#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p489#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p489#2/r1.claim: Nafar denotes a group of between three and ten people.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r1.claim: The surah is difficult because إن recurs with differences between accusative and genitive readings and uncertainty over whether statements belong to God or the jinn, so he explains the whole surah.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r1.anchor: في هذه السورة إشكال وغموض: بما وقع فيها من تكرار (إن) واختلاف القراء في نصبها وكسرها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r2.claim: The jinn listened to the Prophet reciting Quran and, when they returned to their people, told them they had heard a wondrous Quran.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r2.anchor: قال تعالى لنبيه: قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن وكانوا استمعوا لرسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو يقرأ

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r6.claim: He says إن is genitive in all these clauses except أنه استمع.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p241/r6.anchor: وانقطع هاهنا قول الجن. و (إن) في جميع هذا مكسورة إلا (أنه استمع)

NAHHAS:v5p45/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r1.speaker: جوية بن عائذ الأسدي
NAHHAS:v5p45/r1.claim: Juwayya ibn ʿĀʾidh reads أحي إلي, following the dialect of those who say وحى يحي.
NAHHAS:v5p45/r1.anchor: قرأ جوية بن عائذ الأسدي ( قل أحي إلي ) قال أبو جعفر هذا على لغة

NAHHAS:v5p45/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r2.speaker: العجاج
NAHHAS:v5p45/r2.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's poem وحى لها القرار فاستقرت attests the dialectal verb وحى.
NAHHAS:v5p45/r2.anchor: قال العجاج ( وحى لها القرار فاستقرت )

NAHHAS:v5p45/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p45/r3.claim: The underlying form is وحي إلي; hamza replaces initial wāw, as in أقتت.
NAHHAS:v5p45/r3.anchor: والأصل وحي إلي فأبدل من الواو همزة مثل أقتت

NAHHAS:v5p45/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p45/r4.claim: أنه is nominative as the passive subject.
NAHHAS:v5p45/r4.anchor: أنه في موضع رفع اسم مالم يسم فاعله

NAHHAS:v5p45/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p45/r5.claim: Nafar means three or more people.

NAHHAS:v5p45/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p45/r6.claim: إنّ is kasra after saying because it begins a new sentence.
NAHHAS:v5p45/r6.anchor: كسرت ان لأنها بعد القول فهي مبتدأ

NAHHAS:v5p45/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p45/r7.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v5p45/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad says عجب means extraordinary: something rare, scarcely encountered in a like form.
NAHHAS:v5p45/r7.anchor: ومعنى عجب عجيب في اللغة على ما ذكره محمد بن يزيد

SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r1.speaker: العتكي عن أبي عمرو وابن أبي عبلة وأبو إياس
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r1.claim: The common reading is quadriliteral أوحى; al-ʿAtakī from Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Abū Iyās read triliteral وحي, a synonymous form attested by al-ʿAjjāj.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r1.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة أعني كونها من أوحى رباعيا. وقرأ العتكي عن أبي عمرو وابن أبي عبلة وأبو إياس

SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r2.speaker: العجاج
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r2.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's line witnesses the triliteral verb with the sense of revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r2.anchor:
وأنشد للعجاج:
4346 وحى لها القرار فاستقرت

SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي والكسائي وابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r3.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Kisāʾī in one transmission, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla also read أحي, with hamza and no wāw; it replaces initial wāw with hamza and derives from the triliteral variant.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r3.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي والكسائي في رواية وابن أبي عبلة أيضا " أحي " بهمزة مضومة ولا واو بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats hamza-for-wāw substitution as freely regular for wāw with ḍamma, and says al-Māzinī extended it to kasra, citing forms including إعاء أخيه.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وهو من القلب المطلق جوازه في كل واو مضمومة، وقد أطلقه المازني في المكسورة أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r5.claim: The commentator rejects the unrestricted rule: initial, medial, and final wāws have different rules, with details and disagreements among grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وليس كما ذكر، بل في ذلك تفصيل. وذلك أن الواو المضمومة قد تكون أولا وحشوا وآخرا

SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r6.claim: The commentator calls al-Zamakhsharī's discussion self-promoting and states al-Māzinī's two positions; the author defends mentioning the analogy as relevant.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1/r6.anchor: وهذا تكثير وتبجح. وكان يذكر ذلك في سورة يوسف عند قوله

SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r1.claim: أنه استمع is the passive subject because it is the direct object; the Kūfans and al-Akhfash allow the prepositional phrase to serve as passive subject, leaving this accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r1.anchor: هذا هو القائم مقام الفاعل؛ لأنه هو المفعول الصريح، وعند الكوفيين والأخفش يجوز أن يكون القائم مقامه الجار والمجرور

SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r2.claim: من الجن is an adjective modifying نفر.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r2.anchor: و " من الجن " صفة ل " نفر "

SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r3.claim: Describing the Quran as عجَب is hyperbole, an ellipsis for ذا عجب, or a form with the sense of an active participle.
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r3.anchor: ووصف القرآن بعجب: إما على المبالغة، وإما على حذف مضاف، أي: ذا عجب

SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:1#2/r4.claim: يهدي is another adjective modifying قرآنًا.

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r1.claim: The word is read with wāw as awḥiya or without wāw as aḥiya; the latter derives from waḥaytu ilayhi, while awḥaytu is more common.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r1.anchor: القراءة (أوحي) بإثبات الواو. - قد قرئت: (قل أحي إلي) - بغير واو.

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r2.claim: The underlying form is waḥy; wāw with ḍamma may be replaced by hamza, as in ūqqitat from waqt.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r2.anchor: والأصل وحي، ولكن الواو إذا انضمت قد تبدل منها الهمزة نحو: (وإذا الرسل أقتت)

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r3.claim: An exegetical account says the jinn heard the Prophet reciting the dawn prayer at Baṭn Nakhlah; it connects this with the passage saying they were turned toward him and listened.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r3.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن هؤلاء النفر الذين من الجن استمعوا إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r4.claim: When they arrived, some told the others to stop talking and listen.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r4.anchor: أي قال بعضهم لبعض أمسكوا عن الكلام واستمعوا

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r5.claim: Reported identifications differ: some say the jinn came from Naṣībīn and others say Yemen.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r5.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا من جن نصيبين، وقيل إنهم كانوا من اليمن

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r6.claim: Other reports disagree about their religion, identifying them either as Jews or as polytheists.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r6.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يهودا، وقيل إنهم كانوا مشركين

ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r7.claim: The particle an in the clause anna istamaʿa is only read with fatḥa.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233/r7.anchor: فأما قوله: (أنه استمع نفر من الجن)، و (أن) مفتوحة لا غير

ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r1.claim: The particles in innā samiʿnā, fa-inna lahu, and fa-innahu yasluk are all read with kasra.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: (إنا سمعنا) وقوله: (فإن له)، وقوله: (فإنه يسلك). فهذه الثلاث

ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r2.claim: The remaining ann clauses in the sūra have variant readings; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh transmitted from ʿĀṣim like Nāfiʿ, while Ḥafṣ transmitted a kasra where Abū Bakr read a fatḥa.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r2.anchor: فأما عاصم فروى عنه أبوبكر بن عياش مثل قراءة نافع

ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r3.claim: Grammarians prefer Nāfiʿ and his followers: clauses presented as revelation take fatḥa on anna, while the jinn's own statements take kasra, coordinated with their words innā samiʿnā.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r3.anchor: والذي يختاره النحويون قراءة نافع ومن تابعه في هذه الآية عندهم ما كان محمولا على

ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r4.claim: Some grammarians attach the fatḥa construction to the preceding genitive pronoun, but Zajjāj calls that poor analogy because a genitive pronoun should not be coordinated without repeating its preposition.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r4.anchor: ومن فتح فذكر بعض النحويين أنه معطوف على الهاء. المعنى عنده فآمنا به

ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r5.claim: The fatḥa can instead be understood through the sense of āmannā bihi: the meaning is that they believed and affirmed that their Lord's majesty is exalted.
ZAJJAJ:v5p233#2/r5.anchor: ولكن وجهه أن يكون محمولا على معنى آمنا به، لأن معنى آمنا به صدقناه وعلمناه

ASAD-NOTES:72:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:1/r1.claim: The revelation reports that unseen beings listened and described the discourse as wondrous.
ASAD-NOTES:72:1/r1.anchor: some of the unseen beings gave ear

ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r1.claim: In context, istama'a means that the beings both heard and accepted the revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r1.anchor: the meaning, in the above context, of the verbal form istama'a

ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r2.claim: Jinn has several Qur'anic connotations; here it may mean hitherto unseen beings or strangers.
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r2.anchor: the jinn are referred to in the Qur'an in many connotations

ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r3.claim: Asad tentatively reads these beings, as in 46:29–32, as strangers previously unseen by the people receiving the Qur'an.

ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r4.claim: From 46:30 and their rejection of the Trinity at 72:3, Asad infers that they followed Mosaic faith and called the Qur'an a revelation after Moses, omitting Jesus.
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r4.anchor: it transpires that the jinn in question were followers of the Mosaic faith

ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r5.claim: Asad tentatively suggests they may have been Jews from Syria or Mesopotamia.
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r5.anchor: they may have been Jews from distant parts of what is now the Arab world, perhaps from Syria or even Mesopotamia

ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r6.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r6.claim: Tabari says in several places that the jinn in this sūra and 46:29 onward came from Nasibin on the upper Euphrates.
ASAD-NOTES:72:1#n1/r6.anchor: Tabari mentions in several places that the jinn referred to in this surah as well as in 46:29 ff. hailed from Nasibin

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza in four clauses; Nafi and Abu Bakr's Asim transmission agree except they kasra وإنه لما at 72:19, while Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai open all except after speech or a jawab فاء; Hafs matches Hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: قل أوحي إلي أنه [1]، وأن لو استقاموا [16] وأن المساجد لله [18]، وأنه لما قام عبد الله [19] أربعة أحرف بالفتح

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.claim: These four instances of an vary between fatḥa, coordinated with “it was revealed to me,” and kasra, coordinated with “they said: we heard”; after fa in a conditional response, kasra alone is used.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.anchor: هذه الأربعة تقرأ بالفتح وباقي ما قبلها بالكسر فالفتح بالعطف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza in all four cited clauses.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ﴿ قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع ﴾ ﴿ وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.speaker: عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع، والمفضل عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim and Nafi match Abu Amr except that both read the hamza in وأنه لما قام عبد الله with kasra; al-Mufaddal transmits the same from Asim.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع كما قرأ أبو عمرو

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.claim: These readers open the hamza except where the clause follows a statement or a fāʾ of recompense.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم كل ذلك بالفتح إلا ما جاء بعد قول أو بعد فاء جزاء

NASHR:v2p123/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p123/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p123/r2.claim: The ḍamma in “قل أوحي” is transferred from the previous word, so it is an example excluded from the general permission for rūm or ishām.
NASHR:v2p123/r2.anchor: ومثال الحركة المنقولة من كلمة أخرى ضمة اللام في قل أوحي وضمة النون في من أوتي

NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.claim: All agree on fatḥa in annahu istamaʿa and an al-masājidu lillāh because these cannot be the jinn's speech but are revelation; the remaining cases could be either their speech or revelation.
NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.anchor: واتفقوا على فتح أنه استمع، وأن المساجد لله لأنه لا يصح أن يكون من قولهم، بل هو مما أوحي إليه

NASHR:v2p453/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p453/r1.speaker: النبي
NASHR:v2p453/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet promised an answered supplication and a tree in Paradise at Quran completion; al-Bayhaqī grades this chain weak.
NASHR:v2p453/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: " له عند ختم القرآن دعوة مستجابة وشجرة في الجنة "

NASHR:v2p453/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p453/r2.speaker: النبي
NASHR:v2p453/r2.claim: A second weak report from Anas says the Quran's reader receives an answered supplication at completion.
NASHR:v2p453/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: " لصاحب القرآن دعوة مستجابة عند ختمه "

NASHR:v2p453/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p453/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p453/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports rewards of ten good deeds for listening to a letter, fifty or one hundred for reciting in prayer seated or standing, and an answered prayer at completion; al-Bayhaqī says the report is unique through unknown Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar.
NASHR:v2p453/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: " من استمع حرفا

NASHR:v2p453/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p453/r4.speaker: البيهقي
NASHR:v2p453/r4.claim: Al-Bayhaqī says the Ibn ʿAbbās report is uniquely transmitted by Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar, whom he calls unknown.
NASHR:v2p453/r4.anchor: قال البيهقي: تفرد به حفص بن عمر، وهو مجهول

NASHR:v2p122/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p122/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p122/r1.claim: Rawm and ishmām do not apply to a quiescent form, a non-nunated fatḥa, or the hāʾ substituted for feminine tāʾ at pause, since none then bears a recoverable inflectional vowel.
NASHR:v2p122/r1.anchor: الهاء التي تلحق الأسماء في الوقف بدلا من تاء التأنيث نحو الجنة، والملائكة، والقبلة

NASHR:v2p122/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p122/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p122/r2.claim: Plural mīm has no rawm or ishmām at pause whether connected or not; unlike pronoun hāʾ, it lacks a prior vowel, so Makkī's analogy permitting both is invalid.
NASHR:v2p122/r2.anchor: وشذ مكي فأجاز الروم، والإشمام في ميم الجمع لمن وصلها قياسا على هاء الضمير وانتصر لذلك وقواه

NASHR:v2p122/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p122/r3.speaker: مكي
NASHR:v2p122/r3.claim: Makkī permits rawm and ishmām in connected plural mīm by analogy with pronoun hāʾ, but the author rejects this because mīm lacks a prior vowel.
NASHR:v2p122/r3.anchor: وشذ مكي فأجاز الروم، والإشمام في ميم الجمع لمن وصلها قياسا على هاء الضمير

NASHR:v2p122/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p122/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p122/r4.claim: A vowel only present through transfer or meeting two quiescent letters does not permit ishmām when the cause disappears at pause; a kasra intrinsic to the word remains different.
NASHR:v2p122/r4.anchor: المتحرك في الوصل بحركة عارضة إما للنقل نحو وانحر إن، ومن إستبرق، فقد أوتي

NASHR:v2p122/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p122/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p122/r5.claim: For a word connected with kasra, pausing may use sukun or rawm but not ishmām, including transferred kasra and cross-word or tanwīn-induced kasra cases.
NASHR:v2p122/r5.anchor: وهو ما كان في الوصل متحركا بالكسر سواء كانت الكسرة للإعراب أو البناء نحو بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#1/r1.speaker: standard
QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#1/r1.claim: The standard mutawātir form keeps the hamza explicit in pronunciation, reflecting the q-r-ʾ root.
QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#1/r1.anchor: standard, mutawatir: Canonical hamzated surface preserves the explicit ʾ in the q-r-ʾ root during pronunciation

QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#2/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#2/r1.claim: Hamza easing smooths Qurʾānan to Qurānan without changing the analysis of its consonantal root.
QIRAAT-ER:72:1:13#2/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Canonical hamza-eased reading smooths Qurʾānan to Qurānan without changing the consonantal root analysis

IBNHISHAM:v1p204#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p204#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p204#2/r3.claim: After hearing the Quran, the jinn believed, affirmed it, and returned to their people as warners; the passage links their response to the account in 46:29-30.
IBNHISHAM:v1p204#2/r3.anchor: ثم «ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين. قالوا يا قومنا إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى

IBNHISHAM:v1p421#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p421#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p421#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says, as reported to him, that seven jinn from Nisibin heard the Prophet praying at Nakhlah after his return from Taif, believed, and went to warn their people; he connects this to 46:29-31 and 72:1 onward.
IBNHISHAM:v1p421#2/r1.anchor: حتى إذا كان بنخلة قام من جوف الليل يصلي، فمر به النفر من الجن الذين ذكرهم الله تبارك وتعالى، وهم- فيما ذكر لي- سبعة نفر من جن أهل نصيبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r14.claim: After Sūrat Nūḥ, the surah rebukes Quraysh: jinn believed immediately after hearing the Qur’an while Arabs delayed despite recognizing its inimitability.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r14.anchor: أنزل الله تعالى سورة الجن إثر سورة نوح، تبكيتا لقريش والعرب في كونهم تباطؤا عن الإيمان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r1.speaker: زر وعكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r1.claim: Reports give seven or nine jinn; Zarr says three from Ḥarrān and four from Yemeni Nusaybin, while ʿIkrima reports twelve thousand from Mosul.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r1.anchor: الحديث. ويدل على أنهما قصتان، اختلافهم في العدد، فقيل: سبعة، وقيل: تسعة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r2.claim: ʿIkrima’s report of twelve thousand prompts the author to ask how seven and twelve thousand could be reconciled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r2.anchor: وعن عكرمة: كانوا اثني عشر ألفا من جزيرة الموصل، وأين سبعة من اثني عشر ألفا؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r3.claim: After returning to their people, the jinn told them that they had heard a wondrous Qur’an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r3.anchor: فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا: أي قالوا لقومهم لما رجعوا إليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r4.claim: The source-style description intensifies the Qur’an’s wonder: eloquence, fine construction, subtle meanings, unusual style, persuasive admonition, and difference from other books.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r4.anchor: ووصفوا قرآنا بقولهم عجبا وصفا بالمصدر على سبيل المبالغة، أي هو عجب في نفسه لفصاحة كلامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r5.claim: Wonder is something outside its familiar forms and parallels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p293/r5.anchor: والعجب ما خرج عن أحد أشكاله ونظائره.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r1.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة والعتكي عن أبي عمرو وجؤبة بن عائذ الأسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r1.claim: These readers omit the hamza and read waḥy, with the same meaning as ūḥiya; al-ʿAjjāj’s line attests this form.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن أبي عبلة والعتكي عن أبي عمرو وجؤبة بن عائذ الأسدي وحي بلا همزة وهو بمعنى أوحي بالهمز

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي وجؤبة وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r2.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Juʾba in a report from al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Abī ʿAblah in another report read aḥiya, replacing initial wāw with hamza, as in waʿd/aʿd.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وجؤبة فيما روى عنه الكسائي وابن أبي عبلة في رواية أحي بإبدال واو وحي همزة كما قالوا في وعد أعد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls replacing an initial wāw with hamza freely permitted when the wāw is ḍamma-vowelled.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري وهو من القلب المطلق جوازه في كل واو مضمومة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r4.speaker: المازني
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r4.claim: Al-Māzinī extends the change to a kasra-vowelled wāw, citing ishāḥ, iʿāʾ, and isāda; one of his positions restricts it to attested forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r4.anchor: وقد أطلقه المازني في المكسورة أيضا كإشاح وإعاء وإسادة وهذا أحد قولين للمازني والقول الآخر قصر ذلك على السماع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r5.claim: The generalization for ḍamma-vowelled wāw is criticized because initial, medial, and final positions have different rules and disputed details.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r5.anchor: وما ذكره من إطلاق الجواز في المضمومة تعقب بأن المضمومة قد تكون أولا وحشوا وآخرا ولكل منها أحكام وفي بعضها خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r6.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r6.claim: Some eminent grammarians further hold that wāw preceded by ḍamma changes regularly, extending the claim even to a fatḥa context.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r6.anchor: وزاد بعض الأجلة قلب الواو والمضموم ما قبلها فقال أنه أيضا مقيس مطرد وأنه قد يرد في ذلك في المفتوحة كأحد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r7.claim: The phrase “to me” is attached to the passive verb and supplies its deputy subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p81#3/r7.anchor: وعلى جميع القرآن الجار والمجرور متعلق بما عنده ونائب الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r1.claim: The clause beginning anna is interpreted as a verbal noun, and its pronoun refers to the matter being discussed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r1.anchor: على أنه في تأويل المصدر والضمير للشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r2.claim: The object of “listened” is the Qurʾān, omitted because the following words make it clear; al-Aḥqāf supplies this context.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r2.anchor: أي القرآن كما ذكر في الإحقاق وقد حذف لدلالة ما بعده عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r3.claim: Nafar is commonly three to ten, but al-Ḥarīrī wrongly restricts it to three-to-ten men: eloquent usage can exceed ten, as al-Shaʿbī’s “a dozen-odd men” shows.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r3.anchor: النفر في المشهور ما بين الثلاثة والعشرة وقال الحريري في درته أن النفر إنما يقع على الثلاثة من الرجال إلى العشرة وقد وهم في ذلك فقد يطلق على ما فوق العشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r4.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī uses nafar for a dozen-odd people.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r4.anchor: وفي كلام الشعبي حدثني بضعة عشر نفرا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r5.claim: Nafar is not restricted to men or humans, since it is used here of jinn.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r5.anchor: ولا يختص بالرجال بل ولا بالناس لإطلاقه على الجن هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r6.speaker: المجمل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r6.claim: Al-Mujmal says raht and nafar may denote up to forty; raht share one father, unlike nafar.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r6.anchor: وفي المجمل الرهط والنفر يستعمل إلى الأربعين والفرق بينهما أن الرهط يرجعون إلى أب واحد بخلاف النفر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r7.claim: Nafar can also mean a people or group, as in 18:34 and Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r7.anchor: وقد يطلق على القوم ومنه قوله تعالى وأعز نفرا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r8.speaker: الكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r8.claim: Al-Kirmānī records another language usage: nafar can mean one man, as used to explain a sound hadith.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82/r8.anchor: وقال الإمام الكرماني للنفر معنى آخر في العرف وهو الرجل واردا بالعرف عرف اللغة لأنه فسر به الحديث الصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r1.claim: Jinn is singular jinnī, as rūm is singular rūmī.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r2.claim: Jinn are rational bodies dominated by fiery nature, as 55:15 says; another view describes them as airy. All or some can assume different shapes, are usually hidden, and may be seen by prophets and chosen servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r2.anchor: وهم أجسام عاقلة تغلب عليها النارية كما يشهد له قوله تعالى وخلق الجان من مارج من نار وقيل الهوائية قابلة جميعها أو صنف منها للتشكل بالأشكال المختلفة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r3.claim: There is no rational bar to subtle fiery bodies differing in essence from other subtle bodies and receptive to life, power, and extraordinary acts; nature exceeds human understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r3.anchor: ولا مانع عقلا من أن تكون بعض الأجسام اللطيفة النارية مخالفة لسائر أنواع الجسم اللطيف في الماهية ولها قبول لإفاضة الحياة والقدرة على أفعال عجيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r4.claim: Modern philosophers posit subtle bodies with astonishing properties; Al-Ālūsī allows jinn to be bodies of that kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r4.anchor: وقد قال أهل الحكمة الجديدة بأجسام لطيفة أثبتوا لها من الخواص ما يبهر العقول فلتكن أجسام الجن على ذلك النحو

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r5.speaker: ابن سينا
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r5.claim: Most philosophers deny jinn; Ibn Sīnā defines a jinn as an airy animal taking different shapes. Al-Ālūsī treats this as a nominal definition, but says denying external existence is clear unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r5.anchor: وأكثر الفلاسفة على إنكار الجن في رسالة الحدود لابن سينا الجني حيوان هوائي متشكل بأشكال مختلفة وهذا شرح الإسم وظاهره نفي أن يكون لهذه الحقيقة وجود في الخارج ونفي ذلك كفر صريح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r6.speaker: الفلاسفة وأصحاب الروحانيات
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r6.claim: Many ancient philosophers and spiritualists affirm jinn as lower spirits: independent, noncorporeal substances of differing kinds, some good and some evil, whose number only God knows.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r6.anchor: واعترف جمع عظيم من قدماء الفلاسفة وأصحاب الروحانيات بوجودهم ويسمونهم بالأرواح السفلية والمشهور أنهم زعموا أنها جواهر قائمة بأنفسها ليست أجساما ولا جسمانية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r7.claim: One theory says departed human souls gain power and may assist similar later bodies: good souls are angels whose aid is inspiration; evil souls are devils whose aid is temptation. Al-Ālūsī says this conflicts with the Salaf and the apparent Qurʾān and hadith.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r7.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن الأرواح البشرية والنفوس الناطقة إذا فارقت أبدانها ازدادت قوة وكمالا بسبب ما في ذلك العالم الروحاني من انكشاف الأسرار الروحانية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r8.claim: Muslims and most religious communities affirm jinn exist while differing about their nature; Al-Ālūsī directs readers to Ākām al-Marjān and al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr for detail.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p82#2/r8.anchor: والكل مخالف لأقوال السلف وظاهر الآيات والأحاديث وجمهور أرباب الملل معترفون بوجودهم كالمسلمين وإن اختلفوا في حقيقتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r1.speaker: زر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r1.claim: One count gives seven listeners: according to Zirr, three came from Harrān and four from Nusaybin in Yemen, distinct from the Iraqi town.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r1.anchor: فقيل سبعة فعن زر ثلاثة من أهل حران وأربعة من أهل نصيين قرية باليمن غير القرية التي بالعراق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says twelve thousand listeners came from the Island of Mosul; Al-Ālūsī notes that nafar must then mean a group.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r2.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنهم كانوا اثني عشر ألفا من جزيرة الموصل وأين سبعة أو تسعة من اثنتي عشر ألفا ولعل النفر عليه القوم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r3.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the jinn were from Shayṣabān, the largest jinn tribe and source of most of Iblīs’s troops.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r3.anchor: وفي الكشاف كانوا من الشيصبان وهم أكثر الجن عددا وعامة جنود إبليس منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r4.claim: The wording suggests the Prophet learned of the jinn’s listening by revelation, not direct observation; reports that he saw them are reconciled as separate incidents.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r4.anchor: والآية ظاهر في أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم علم استماعهم له بالوحي لا بالمشاهدة وقد وقع في الأحاديث أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام رآهم وجمع ذلك بتعدد القصة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r5.claim: In a Ṣaḥīḥayn account, Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet neither recited to jinn nor saw them on that occasion: while companions traveled to ʿUkāẓ, a group barred from heaven by meteors heard his dawn prayer at Nakhlah and returned to warn their people.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r5.anchor: في الصحيحين في حديث ابن عباس ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على الجن ولا رآهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r6.speaker: البيهقي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqī reconciles Ibn ʿAbbās’s limited denial with 46:29, which says the Prophet spoke with the jinn, called them, and made them messengers to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r6.anchor: ونفى ابن عباس إنما هو في هذه القصة واستماعهم تلاوته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في الفجر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r7.claim: Abū Dāwūd transmits from ʿAlqama, from Ibn Masʿūd, that a jinn caller came to the Prophet, who went with him, recited Qurʾān, and was shown their traces and fires.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r7.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن علقمة عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال أتاني داعي الجن فذهبت معه وقرأت عليهم القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r8.speaker: ابن تيمية
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r8.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says Ibn ʿAbbās knew Qurʾānic evidence but not what Ibn Masʿūd and Abū Hurayra knew about jinn visiting and speaking with the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r8.anchor: وقال ابن تيمية أن ابن عباس علم ما دل عليه القرآن ولم يعلم ما علمه ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r9.speaker: الواقدي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r9.claim: The encounter is dated three years before the Hijra; al-Wāqidī places it in Prophethood’s eleventh year, when Ibn ʿAbbās was near adolescence at the Farewell Pilgrimage. Al-Ālūsī says six visits explain differing accounts.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r9.anchor: وقصة الجن كانت قبل الهجرة بثلاث سنين وقال الواقدي كانت سنة إحدى عشرة من النبوة وابن عباس ناهز الحلم في حجة الوداع فقد علمت أن قصة الجن وقعت ست مرات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r10.claim: Al-Bayhaqī cites Ibn Masʿūd: after ʿishāʾ the Prophet led him to a place, drew a line he must not cross, then met jinn resembling Zutt; returning near dawn, he said the voices were jinn bidding him farewell and greeting.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83/r10.anchor: وفي شرح البيهقي من طرق شتى عن ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم صلى العشاء ثم انصرف فأخذ بيدي حتى أتينا مكان كذا فأجلسني وخط علي خطا ثم قال لا تبرحن خطك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r1.claim: ʿIkrima identifies what the jinn heard as “Read in the name of your Lord.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r1.anchor: واختلف فيما استمعوه فقال عكرمة اقرأ باسم ربك وقيل سورة الرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r2.claim: An unnamed view says they heard Sūrat al-Raḥmān.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r2.anchor: واختلف فيما استمعوه فقال عكرمة اقرأ باسم ربك وقيل سورة الرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r3.claim: “Qurʾān” here means a recited book, one of the heavenly scriptures; this wording encompasses the qualities they go on to describe.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r3.anchor: أي كتابا مقروءا على ما فسره بعض الأجلة وفسر بذلك للإشارة إلى ما ذكروه في وصفه مما يأتي له كله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r4.claim: The indefinite noun is for magnification: they heard a Qurʾān of great standing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r4.anchor: والتنوين للتفخيم أي قرآنا جليل الشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r5.claim: “Wondrous” means strikingly novel, unlike human speech in its beautiful arrangement and subtle meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r5.anchor: بديعا مباينا لكلام الناس في حسن النظم ودقة المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p83#2/r6.claim: The verbal noun “wonder” is used adjectivally for emphasis.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r1.claim: The jinn group consisted of nine from Nasibin; another account says seven heard the Prophet reciting, with their story also told in al-Ahqaf.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r1.anchor: وكانوا تسعة من جن نصيبين. وقيل سبعة استمعوا قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرنا خبرهم في سورة الأحقاف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the Quran eloquent and wondrous, astonishing because of its eloquence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p235#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بليغا أي: قرآنا ذا عجب يعجب منه لبلاغته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.claim: Uthman reports the Prophet said the best people learn and teach the Qur’an; al-Baghawi calls the report authentic and says al-Bukhari transmitted it via Hajjaj ibn Minhal from Shuʿba.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ قال: نعم قال: " خيركم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet identifies the Qur’an as the refuge from tribulation, containing news of past and future and judgment between people; it is decisive, not a jest.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ألا إنها ستكون فتنة قلت فما المخرج منها يا رسول الله؟ قال: كتاب الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.claim: Ali reports the Prophet warns abandoning Qur’an crushes tyrants and those seeking guidance elsewhere go astray. It is God’s firm rope, wise reminder and straight path, unbent by whims/tongues; scholars never tire, repetition cannot wear it out, wonders never end.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ألا إنها ستكون فتنة قلت فما المخرج منها يا رسول الله؟ قال: كتاب الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.speaker: الجن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.claim: The jinn who heard the Qur’an said it was amazing, guided to right conduct, and they believed in it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.anchor: هو الذي لم تنته الجن إذ سمعته حتى قالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.speaker: أبو عيسى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.claim: Abu Isa says the report is known only through this route, its chain is unknown, and al-Harith is criticized.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو عيسى: هذا (الحديث) لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه وإسناده مجهول، والحارث فيه مقال

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Jinn is Meccan and has twenty-eight verses.

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r2.claim: The verb is also read “أحي” or in its original form “وحي”; the hamza replaces wāw because of its ḍamma.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r2.anchor: وقرىء «أحي» وأصله وحى من وحى إليه فقلبت الواو همزة لضمتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r3.claim: The clause “that a group of jinn listened” is the subject of the verb “was revealed.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r3.anchor: وفاعله: { أنه استمع نفر من الجن }

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r4.claim: Nafar denotes a group of between three and ten.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r4.anchor: والنفر ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r5.claim: Jinn are intelligent, hidden beings, predominantly fiery or airy; alternatives identify them as separate spirits or human souls separated from bodies.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r5.anchor: وقيل نوع من الأرواح المجردة وقيل نفوس بشرية مفارقة عن أبدانها

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r6.claim: The Prophet did not see the jinn or recite directly to them; they happened to hear one of his recitations, and God informed him of it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r6.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما رآهم ولم يقرأ عليهم وإنما اتفق حضورهم في بعض أوقات قراءته فسمعوها فأخبر الله به رسوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r7.claim: The jinn spoke after returning to their people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r9.claim: The Qurʾān is wondrous and unlike human speech in the beauty of its arrangement and precision of meaning; the verbal noun is used adjectivally for emphasis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:1/r9.anchor: بديعا مباينا لكلام الناس في حسن نظمه ودقة معناه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.claim: The opening contrasts Noah’s idol-worshipping, disobedient people and Muhammad’s similarly hostile Arabs with jinn who readily accept the final, comprehensive revelation, rebuking the Arabs’ delay despite their shared language and kinship with Muhammad.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.anchor: ابتدئت , هذه بما كان من سهولة من سمع هذه الدعوة الخاتمة الجامعة من غير الجنس فضلا عن الموافقين في الجنس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.claim: The command is for Muhammad to address his people with this news.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.claim: The passive wording gives prominence to the revelation, since the revealer of both messengers is one.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.anchor: المقصود تعظيم الموحى به , وأما الموحي إلى كل من الرسولين فواحد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.claim: Muhammad was secretly informed by the sole knower of the unseen through Gabriel; the Quran’s inimitability portends that he will have the most followers among prophets.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.anchor: أخبرت على وجه الخفاء ممن لا يعلم الغيب غيره في هذا القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.claim: The jinn listened with exceptional attentiveness, receptivity, acceptance, and familiarity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.anchor: بغاية الإصغاء والإقبال والتقبل والإلف استماعا هو الاستماع في الحقيقة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.claim: Jinn are living, rational bodies, predominantly fiery or airy, unlike humans, whose predominant nature is earthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.anchor: الذين هم في غاية الاستتار , وهم أجسام حية عاقلة خفيفة تغلب عليها النارية أو الهوائية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r7.claim: Nafar denotes a group of between three and ten.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r8.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r8.claim: Al-Baghawi says the group consisted of nine jinn from Nasibin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r8.anchor: قال البغوي : وكانوا تسعة من جن نصيبين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r9.claim: Another reported view counts seven jinn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : كانوا سبعة , وفي هذه العبارة دليل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r10.claim: The wording indicates Muhammad neither saw the jinn nor recited to them; they happened to be present when he recited.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r10.anchor: وفي هذه العبارة دليل على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ما رآهم ولا قرأ عليهم , وإنما اتفق حضورهم عند قراءته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan says the well-known view identifies this listening with the jinn’s listening in al-Ahqaf.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو حيان : المشهور أنه هو , وقيل : هو غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r12.claim: The hadith evidence appears to indicate more than one encounter; one group came at Mecca from Nasibin and another at Nakhla from Nineveh.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r12.anchor: ويظهر من الحديث تعدد الواقعة , فمنها ما كان في المبدأ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r13.speaker: عكرمة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r13.claim: Ikrimah says the jinn heard Surat al-Alaq.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r13.anchor: والسورة التي استمعوها قال عكرمة : العلق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r14.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r14.claim: Another view says the recited surah was al-Rahman.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r15.claim: In a report in al-Sahih, the Prophet was missing one night; a caller from the jinn came, he went with them and recited Quran, then they showed him their tracks and fires.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r15.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه الذي في الصحيح ( أنهم فقدوه صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة من الليالي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r16.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r16.claim: In another report, Ibn Masud accompanied the Prophet to al-Hajun; the Prophet drew a boundary, recited to jinn hidden from Ibn Masud, and signaled him to remain seated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r16.anchor: ومنها ما كان معه عبد الله رضي الله عنه فذهب معه إلى الحجون عند الشعب فخط عليه خطا , وقال : لا تجاوزه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r17.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r17.claim: Al-Asbahani says they belonged to Banu al-Shaysaban, the most numerous jinn and the main body of Satan’s troops.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r17.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : وقيل : كانوا من بني الشيصبان وهم أكثر الجن عددا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r18.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r18.claim: Al-Qushayri says seven jinn came to Nakhla after the devils were pelted with meteors, believed, and told their people; later seventy from their people came to the Prophet and converted.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p180#2/r18.anchor: وقال القشيري : لما رجمت الشياطين بالشهب فرق إبليس جنوده لعلم ذلك فأتى سبعة منهم بطن نخلة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r1.claim: The listeners reported to those among the jinn who had not heard, or to their human allies, following the prophetic instruction to convey what one hears.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r1.anchor: فقالوا } أي فتسبب عن استماعهم أن قال من سمع منهم لمن لم يسمع , أو لمن كان يواخيهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r2.claim: The Prophet prayed for the one who hears, understands, and conveys a saying as heard; no grading is stated here.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r2.anchor: لقوله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رحم الله امرأ سمع منا مقالة فوعاها فأداها كما سمعها )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r3.claim: Inna is read with kasra because it begins a quoted statement after the verb of saying.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r3.anchor: بالكسر لأنه مبتدأ محكي بعد القول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r4.claim: They deliberately listened, turned their attention to the Quran, and were struck by it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r4.anchor: حين تعمدنا الإصغاء وألقينا إليه فأهامنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r5.claim: They call it speech exceptionally well ordered in itself and comprehensive of everything people need.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r5.anchor: كلاما هو في غاية الانتظام في نفسه والجمع لجميع ما نحتاج إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r6.claim: Calling the Quran ajab as a verbal noun intensifies its description: it is unprecedented and its cause is hidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r6.anchor: بالمصدر مبالغة في أمره فقالوا : { عجبا * } أي بديعا خارجا عن عادة أمثاله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r7.claim: Its arrangement, composition, and diction exceed divine books and human speech, while agreeing with scripture in calling to God, distinguishing good from evil, and summoning people to salvation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r7.anchor: في جلالة النظم وإعجاز التركيب والوضع مع الموافقة لها في الدعوة إلى الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r8.claim: The jinn’s description shows their eloquence and command of rhetorical composition as well as their intellectual strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r8.anchor: وهذا يدل على قوتهم العلمية في فصاحتهم وكمالهم في علم الرسوم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r9.speaker: الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r9.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links this opening to the preceding surahs: after Quraysh’s obstinacy, the warning of al-Haqqah, its confirmation in al-Maarij, and consolation through Noah, the jinn’s response teaches the receptive that hearts are in God’s hands.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p182/r9.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تقدم ذكر حال كفار قريش في تعاميهم عن النظر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p183/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p183/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p183/r1.claim: The account continues the jinn’s story from al-Ahqaf and connects it to their later report about the Arab unbelievers’ opposition to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p183/r1.anchor: إلى قوله إخبارا عن تعريف الجن سائر أخوانهم بما شاهدوه من عنااد كفار العرب

DURR-FULL:v8p296/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has twenty-eight verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p296/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير وعائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Aisha each report that Sūrat al-Jinn was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة الجن بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p296/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after devils were barred from sky-news and pelted by meteors, their people sent groups across the earth to discover what had changed.
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: انطلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ وقد حيل بين الشياطين وبين خبر السماء وأرسلت عليهم الشهب

DURR-FULL:v8p296/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says a party searching toward Tihama found the Prophet at Nakhlah praying Fajr; they listened and realized his recitation explained the obstruction to the sky.
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: انطلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ

DURR-FULL:v8p296/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the jinn returned announcing that the wondrous Qurʾan guides to right guidance and that they believed; God revealed the jinn’s statement to the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: انطلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ

DURR-FULL:v8p296/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r6.speaker: عبد الملك
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r6.claim: Abd al-Malik says heaven was unguarded between Jesus and Muhammad; after Muhammad’s mission it was guarded and meteors sent against jinn, so Iblis dispatched leading jinn to Tihama and Yemen, where seven from Nasibin heard the Prophet at Nakhlah and returned as believers.
DURR-FULL:v8p296/r6.anchor: عن عبد الملك قال: لم تحرس الجن في الفترة بين عيسى ومحمد

DURR-FULL:v8p297/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p297/r1.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v8p297/r1.claim: Sahl says he met a huge jinn elder praying toward the Kaaba in a wool cloak said to be seven hundred years old; the elder blamed clothing wear on sinful smells and unlawful food and said he had met and believed in Jesus and Muhammad, among the Nasibin jinn.
DURR-FULL:v8p297/r1.anchor: عن سهل بن عبد الله قال: كنت في ناحية ديار عاد إذا رأيت مدينة من حجر منقورة في وسطها قصر من حجارة تأويه الجن

BUKHARI:4921/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4921/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BUKHARI:4921/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that jinn, blocked from heavenly news, heard Muhammad reciting at Nakhlah and returned to their people with the message; the sura’s opening was revealed as the jinn’s own account of what they heard.
BUKHARI:4921/r1.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ انْطَلَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي طَائِفَةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ

IBNHIBBAN:6526/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6526/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNHIBBAN:6526/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet neither addressed nor saw the jinn; a group heard him reciting at dawn near Nakhla, recognized the Quran as what blocked their access to heavenly news, and reported their belief to their people.
IBNHIBBAN:6526/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن، وما رآهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r1.claim: The sūra is called al-Jinn in tafsīr works and manuscripts, by al-Tirmidhī, and popularly “Qul ūḥiya”; al-Bukhārī titles it “Sūrat Qul ūḥiya.” Both names are apt, though al-Itqān does not list it among multiply named sūras.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r1.anchor: في كتب التفسير وفي المصاحف التي رأيناها ومنها الكوفي المكتوب بالقيروان في القرن الخامس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r2.claim: The sūra is Meccan by consensus.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r3.claim: A report in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and al-Tirmidhī says the Prophet and companions headed toward the ʿUkāẓ market at Nakhlah; while he prayed dawn, jinn listened and returned to tell their people they had heard wondrous Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r3.anchor: من حديث ابن عباس أنه قال : انطلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq places the revelation after the Prophet’s trip to al-Ṭāʾif seeking support from Thaqīf, in the tenth year of the mission, three years before the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r4.anchor: ذكر ابن إسحاق أن نزول هذه السورة كان بعد سفر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الطائف يطلب النصرة من ثقيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r5.claim: The sūra is the fortieth in revelation order, after al-Aʿrāf and before Yā-Sīn; scholars agree it has twenty-eight verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p216/r5.anchor: وقد عدت السورة الأربعين في نزول السور نزلت بعد الأعراف وقبل يس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r1.claim: The wording implies that the Prophet learned of the jinn’s listening only through God’s revelation, not before the verse was sent down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r1.anchor: إيماء إلى أنه ما علم بذلك إلا بإخبار الله إياه بوقوع هذا الاستماع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r2.claim: The Ahqāf passage (46:29–30) may recall this event, or may refer to a separate story reported by Ibn Masʿūd in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim about recitation in prayers; Ibn Ashur says that story is unrelated to this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r2.anchor: فتذكير بما في هذه الآية أو هي إشارة إلى قصة أخرى رواها عبد الله بن مسعود وهي في صحيح مسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r3.claim: The clause that a group listened is the passive subject of “it was revealed to me,” meaning that their listening was revealed to the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r3.anchor: في موضع نائب فاعل { أوحي } أي أوحي إلي استماع نفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r4.claim: The particle anna emphasizes the revealed report because it is extraordinary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r4.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر الموحى بحرف ( أن ) للاهتمام به لغرابته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r5.claim: The pronoun in anna is a pronoun of the affair, with the following sentence as its predicate, further stressing the revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r5.anchor: وضمير { أنه } ضمير الشأن وخبره جملة { استمع نفر من الجن }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r6.claim: The object of “listened” is omitted and supplied by the jinn’s statement: they listened to the Qur’an.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r7.claim: Nafar means a group of one to ten; it normally denotes humans, but is analogically applied to jinn for lack of another word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r7.anchor: النفر : الجماعة من واحد إلى عشرة وأصله في اللغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r8.claim: Likewise, “men” in 72:6 denotes jinn persons, using a human term for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r8.anchor: كما أطلق رجال في قوله : { يعوذون برجال من الجن }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r9.claim: They said this to members of their kind who were absent; God inspired them to warn and guide them, as elaborated in 46:29–30.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r9.anchor: قالوه لبعض منهم لم يحضر لاستماع القرآن ألهمهم الله أن ينذروهم ويرشدوهم إلى الصلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r10.claim: “They said” means conveying their intent in the mode by which they communicate, since jinn apparently do not use words spoken on tongues; it is a figurative use like the ant’s speech in 27:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r10.anchor: ومعنى القول هنا : إبلاغ مرادهم إلى من يريدون أن يبلغوه إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r11.claim: The Qur’an’s metaphorical use of speech, like the ant’s communication in 27:18, dignifies Islam by giving it callers from both kinds of beings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p219/r11.anchor: فيكون ذلك تكريما لهذا الدين أن جعل الله له دعاة من الثقلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r1.claim: The majority read أوحي, from أوحى يوحي.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r1.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «قل أوحي إلي» من أوحى يوحي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r2.speaker: جوية بن عائذ
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r2.claim: Juwayya read أوحى, deriving it from وحي يحي and treating the forms as synonymous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو أناس جوية بن عائذ: «قل أوحى إلي» ، من وحي يحي ووحي وأوحى، بمعنى واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r3.speaker: العجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r3.claim: Al-Ajjaj's line supplies poetic evidence for the form وحي.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r4.speaker: جوية بن عائذ، ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r4.claim: Juwayya, as transmitted by al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Abi Abla read أحي, substituting hamza for waw as in وسادة وإسادة.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r4.anchor: قرأ أيضا جوية فيما روى عنه الكسائي، «قل أحي» أبدلت الواو همزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Abla also reads أحي with hamza substituted for waw.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari reports that Asim kasra-reads every initial إن/أن in the surah except the clause at 72:18.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.anchor: حكى الطبري عن عاصم أنه كان يكسر كل ألف في السورة من «أن» و «إن» إلا قوله تعالى: وأن المساجد لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r7.claim: A report says Abu Amr kasra-read from the surah's start through 72:16 and opened the hamza thereafter; Ibn Atiyya says this report is unestablished because it entails kasra at 72:1.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r7.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو أنه يكسر من أولها إلى قوله وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi reports that Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open four hamzas in the surah and kasra-read the others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.anchor: وذكر أبو علي الفارسي أن ابن كثير وأبا عمرو فتحا أربعة أحرف من السورة وكسرا غير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.speaker: ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي، حفص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.claim: These readers open the surah's hamzas except after a saying or a consequential fa; this yields consensus on openings at 72:1, 72:16, and 72:18.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.anchor: وذكر أن ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي كانوا يقرأون كل ما في السورة بالفتح إلا ما جاء بعد قول أو فاء جزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r11.speaker: علقمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r11.claim: Al-Zahrawi reports that Alqama opened the hamza throughout the surah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r11.anchor: وذكر الزهراوي عن علقمة أنه كان يفتح الألف في السورة كلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.claim: Abu Hatim explains opening as coordination under passive أوحي, with clauses in the nominative; kasra is quotation, resumption, or follows a saying.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: أما الفتح فعلى أوحي، فهو كله في موضع رفع على ما لم يسم فاعله. وأما الكسر فحكاية وابتداء وبعد القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r13.claim: These jinn encountered the Prophet reciting the dawn prayer at Nakhlah on his way to Ukaz; their story was treated under 46:29.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r13.anchor: وهؤلاء النفر من الجن هم الذين صادفوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ ببطن نخلة في صلاة الصبح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.claim: With the opening reading, 72:19 is coordinated with 72:1; some identify the servant as Noah and those nearly crowding him as his disbelieving people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء على ما تقدم «وأنه» بفتح الألف، وهذا عطف على قوله أنه استمع

MUSLIM:1006/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:1006/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSLIM:1006/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that jinn, blocked from heavenly news, heard the Prophet reciting at dawn near Nakhlah, believed, and told their people; the report connects this event to the revelation of 72:1.
MUSLIM:1006/r1.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ مَا قَرَأَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى الْجِنِّ وَمَا رَآهُمُ انْطَلَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r1.claim: The occasion of the jinn listening is explained at 46:29, where the account and number of the jinn are also discussed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r1.anchor: قد ذكرنا سبب نزول هذه الآية في الأحقاف 29 وبينا هنالك سبب استماعهم ومعنى النفر وعددهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r2.claim: “A wondrous Qurʾān” means eloquent, astonishing because of its eloquence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p377/r2.anchor: فأما قوله تعالى قرآنا عجبا فمعناه بليغا يعجب منه لبلاغته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p237#4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p237#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p237#4/r1.claim: God commands the Messenger to tell his people that a group of jinn heard the Quran, believed and submitted to it; its guidance leads to right conduct and success, and they will associate no one with their Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p237#4/r1.anchor: أي: إلى السداد والنجاح، {فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:2271/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2271/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2271/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet neither recited to nor saw the jinn; on a journey toward Ukaz, jinn heard his dawn recitation, identified it as the cause of the blocked heavenly news, and reported the wondrous Qur'an, after which this revelation recounted their words.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2271/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن، ولا رآهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that God listens to no recitation as He listens to a prophet reciting the Quran; Muslim and al-Nasa'i transmit this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r1.anchor: أنه كان يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r2.speaker: صاحبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r2.claim: An unnamed transmitter glosses the Prophet's phrase as reciting the Quran aloud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r2.anchor: وقال صاحب له: يريد يجهر به فرد من هذا الوجه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r3.speaker: سفيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r3.claim: Sufyan explains the phrase as finding sufficiency in the Quran.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the hadith as God's special attention to a prophet who recites aloud beautifully; prophets combine a fine voice with complete reverence and excellent constitution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r4.anchor: ومعناه: أن الله ما استمع لشيء كاستماعه لقراءة نبي يجهر بقراءته ويحسنها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r5.claim: Aisha said that God's hearing encompasses all sounds; Ibn Kathir says He hears all servants but attends more closely to believers' Quran recitation, and most closely to prophets' recitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r5.anchor: كما قالت عائشة، رضي الله عنها: سبحان الله الذي وسع سمعه الأصوات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers interpreting udhn here as listening rather than command, based on the immediate context and the sky and earth listening to God in 84:1-5.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r6.anchor: ومنهم من فسر الأذن هاهنا بالأمر، والأول أولى لقوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r7.claim: A good-chain report from Fadala ibn Ubayd compares God's listening to a man with a beautiful voice reciting aloud to a songstress listening to her singer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p59/r7.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r1.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that the Prophet told Quran students to learn and acquire the Book, and the narrator was unsure whether he also said to recite it melodiously.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r1.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر قال: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r2.claim: A second route through Musa ibn Ali says without uncertainty, acquire the Quran and recite it melodiously; Ahmad and al-Nasa'i transmit both routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r2.anchor: من حديث موسى بن علي، عن أبيه به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r3.claim: A version in which the Prophet greets people reading Quran supports greeting a person who is reciting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r3.anchor: وفي بعض ألفاظه: خرج علينا ونحن نقرأ القرآن فسلم علينا، وذكر الحديث.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r4.claim: Al-Muhasir ibn Habib reports in a mursal narration: people of the Quran should not use it as a pillow, should recite it at all hours, acquire it, and reflect on it for success.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r4.anchor: عن المهاصر بن حبيب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r5.claim: Abu Ubayd glosses taghannawhu as making Quran one's sufficiency instead of poverty, and iqtanuhu as acquiring it like wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r5.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبيد: قوله: "تغنوه": يعني: اجعلوه غناءكم من الفقر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd transmits Fadala's report that God listens especially to a man with a beautiful Quran voice; Ibn Majah's route adds that he recites aloud and includes Maysara, Fadala's client, in the chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: حدثني هشام بن عمار، عن يحيى بن حمزة، عن الأوزاعي، حدثني إسماعيل ابن عبيد الله بن أبي المهاجر، عن فضالة بن عبيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd says the phrase about God granting permission means that God listens.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p60/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: يعني: الاستماع. وقوله في الحديث الآخر:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r1.claim: Umar used to ask Abu Musa to remind them of their Lord, after which Abu Musa recited for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r1.anchor: عن أبي سلمة قال: كان عمر إذا رأى أبا موسى قال: ذكرنا ربنا يا أبا موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r2.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said Abu Musa's prayer-leading voice sounded more beautiful than any cymbal, lute, or other sound he had heard.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r2.anchor: كان أبو موسى يصلي بنا، فلو قلت: إني لم أسمع صوت صنج قط، ولا بربط قط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r3.claim: Aisha says she heard an unusually beautiful recitation from a Companion, and the Prophet went with her to listen and identified the reader as Salim, client of Abu Hudhayfa; Ibn Kathir grades the chain good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r3.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: " أبطأت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة بعد العشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r4.claim: The Prophet praised God for placing a reciter like Salim in his community.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r4.anchor: هذا سالم مولى أبي حذيفة، الحمد لله الذي جعل في أمتي مثل هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r5.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r5.claim: Jubayr heard the Prophet recite al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer and said no one recited more beautifully; the verse about creation made him feel his heart would split.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r5.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن جبير بن مطعم قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في المغرب بالطور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r6.claim: Jubayr was still a polytheist when he heard this, arriving later after Badr to ransom captives; Ibn Kathir says the recitation caused his guidance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r6.anchor: وكان جبير لما سمع هذا بعد مشركا على دين قومه، وإنما قدم في فداء الأسارى بعد بدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r7.claim: The best Quran recitation is rooted in a reverent heart, not merely a pleasant voice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r7.anchor: ولهذا كان أحسن القراءة ما كان عن خشوع القلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r8.speaker: طاوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r8.claim: Tawus says the person with the best Quran voice is the one most fearful of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r8.anchor: عن ليث، عن طاوس قال: أحسن الناس صوتا بالقرآن أخشاهم لله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r9.claim: In a report through Tawus, the Prophet says the best Quran voice belongs to the person whose recitation makes a listener see that he fears God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p63/r9.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، وعن الحسن بن مسلم، عن طاوس قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.claim: Harith al-A'war reports that Gabriel told the Prophet his community would differ; the Quran is the refuge that saves whoever clings to it and destroys any tyrant who abandons it, and its marvels do not end.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.anchor: قال: ثم قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.claim: Ali reports the Prophet describing the Quran as the account of past peoples, news of the future, and judgment among people; it is the decisive word, an unbreakable rope, a straight path, and never exhausted by repetition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.anchor: أما إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb, says it is known only through Hamza al-Zayyat, and judges its chain unknown, adding that Harith's report is criticized.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.anchor: ثم قال: هذا حديث غريب لا نعرفه إلا من حديث حمزة الزيات، وإسناده مجهول وفي حديث الحارث مقال

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Jinn is Meccan and has twenty-eight verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmits a Prophetic merit report: reciting the sura frees a slave for each jinn or devil who believed in Muhammad or rejected him; no grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r2.anchor: عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما رواه أبي بن كعب:

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r3.claim: After Noah’s people followed leaders of misguidance, this sura contrasts jinn following the Messenger.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r3.anchor: ولما تقدم في سورة (نوح) اتباع القوم أكابرهم ورؤساء الضلال والكفر، ولم يتبعوا نوحا،

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open four specified particles; other forms are kasra.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: أوحي إلي أنه، وألو استقاموا، وأن المساجد، وأنه لما قام هذه الأربعة الأحرف بفتح الألف،

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r5.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r5.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr from Asim follow that pattern except wa-innahu la-mma qāma is kasra.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم كذلك، إلا قوله: وإنه لما قام عبد الله فإنهما كسراه.

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar opens the initial annahu and specified later clauses, kasrates wa-innā ẓanannā, and details other readings.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع بالفتح، ولم يختلفوا فيه،

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r7.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r7.claim: Ibn Amir, Hafs from Asim, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf open the initial annahu and following forms through wa-annahu la-mma qāma.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف: قل أوحي إلي أنه بفتح الألف،

JISHUMI:v10p7107/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r8.claim: Open forms coordinate with “I was revealed”; kasra coordinates with “they said, we heard,” since reported speech begins a new utterance.
JISHUMI:v10p7107/r8.anchor: والأصل فيه أن كل من نصب فهو عطف على قوله: (أوحي إلي أنه)، ومن كسر فهو عطف على قوله: (فقالوا إنا سمعنا)

JISHUMI:v10p7110/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r1.claim: The passive leaves the agent unnamed as a mark of glorification.
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r1.anchor: قل يا محمد أوحي ذكره على ما لم يسم فاعله تفخيما وتعظيما،

JISHUMI:v10p7110/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r2.claim: Nafar is a group of men; a report says seven jinn from Nasibin listened to the Prophet and returned home.
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r2.anchor: والنفر يكون من الرجال، قيل: كانوا سبعة من نصيبين، استمعوا قراءة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -،

JISHUMI:v10p7110/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
