JISHUMI:v10p7110/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r3.claim: The Qur’an is astonishing either because it is miraculous or because its structure, eloquence, and meaning are extraordinary.
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r3.anchor: قيل معجزا؛ لأن كلام العباد لا يتعجب منه، وقيل: أرادوا كلاما خارجا عن المعتاد نظما وفصاحة ومعنى

JISHUMI:v10p7110/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r7.claim: Some say the Prophet did not see the jinn; others say he saw seven from Nasibin and sent them to other jinn.
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r7.anchor: لذلك قال: (قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع)، وقيل: بل رآهم، وكانوا سبعة رهط من جن نصيبين،

JISHUMI:v10p7110/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r8.claim: Ibn Masud saw Zutt and said they resembled jinn he had seen on the Night of the Jinn.
JISHUMI:v10p7110/r8.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أنه رأى قوما من الزط، فقال: ما أشبههم بالجن الذين رأيتهم ليلة الجن،

TIRMIDHI:3323/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3323/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TIRMIDHI:3323/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet neither recited to nor saw the jinn: a group heard him praying at Nakhla, believed, and their declaration was revealed in 72:1. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
TIRMIDHI:3323/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، رضى الله عنهما قال ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن ولا رآهم انطلق رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r1.claim: أوحي is related to وحى by replacing initial wāw with hamza, like أعد and أزن; this substitution is freely allowed when wāw has ḍamma.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r1.anchor: قرىء ( أحى ) وأصله وحي ؛ يقال : أوحي إليه ووحى إليه ، فقلبت الواو همزة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r2.claim: The same substitution appears in 77:11; al-Mazini also permits it with kasra and cites forms such as إشاح and إسادة.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r2.anchor: كما يقال : أعد وأزن { وإذا الرسل أقتت }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads وحى, retaining the original form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( وحى ) على الأصل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r4.claim: Open أنَّهُ because its clause is the subject of أوحي; kasra in إنا سمعنا marks an independent clause quoted after قالوا.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r4.anchor: { أنه استمع } بالفتح ، لأنه فاعل أوحى . وإنا سمعنا : بالكسر ؛ لأنه مبتدأ محكي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r5.claim: Other clauses attributed to revelation take fatḥa and those spoken by the jinn take kasra, except the last two clauses in verses 18 and 19.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r5.anchor: فما كان من الوحي فتح ، وما كان من قول الجن كسر : وكلهن من قولهم إلا الثنتين الأخريين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r6.claim: Those who read all clauses with fatḥa coordinate them with the syntactic position of آمنا به, as if the jinn believed the following claims too.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r6.anchor: ومن فتح كلهن فعطفا على محل الجار والمجرور في آمنا به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r7.claim: نفر means a group numbering from three to ten.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r7.anchor: جماعة منهم ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r8.claim: It is said that the group belonged to the Shaysaban, the most numerous jinn and the main body of Iblis's troops.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r8.anchor: وقيل : كانوا من الشيصبان ، وهم أكثر الجن عددا وعامة جنود إبليس منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r9.claim: They spoke to their people after returning, as the account in 46:29–30 also says.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r9.anchor: أي : قالوا لقومهم حين رجعوا إليهم ، كقوله : { فلما قضى ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r10.claim: The Qur'an is unlike other books in the beauty of its composition and soundness of meaning, and contains proofs of its inimitability.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r10.anchor: بديعا مباينا لسائر الكتب في حسن نظمه وصحة معانيه ، قائمة فيه دلائل الإعجاز

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r11.claim: عجب is a verbal noun used in place of عجيب, with emphatic force.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p625/r11.anchor: وعجب مصدر يوضع موضع العجيب . وفيه مبالغة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود والضحاك وطائفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r1.claim: One account says God directed the jinn to the Prophet, as in 46:29.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن الله تعالى صرفهم إليه بقوله : ^ { وإذا صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن } ^ [ الأحقاف : 29 ] , قاله ابن مسعود والضحاك وطائفة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r2.claim: One account says jinn had listened from stations in the lowest heaven until Muhammad's mission brought heavenly guarding and shooting stars.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان للجن مقاعد في السماء الدنيا يستمعون منها ما يحدث فيها من أمور الدنيا , فلما بعث الله رسوله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم حرست السماء الدنيا من الجن ورجموا بالشهب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the sky had only been guarded when a prophet or a manifest sign of one was present on earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r3.anchor: قال السدي : ولم تكن السماء تحرس إلا أن يكون في الأرض نبي أو أثر له ظاهر , قال :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r4.claim: When people of Taif saw the shooting stars, they feared the people of heaven had perished and began freeing slaves and releasing livestock.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r4.anchor: قال السدي : ولم تكن السماء تحرس إلا أن يكون في الأرض نبي أو أثر له ظاهر , قال : فلما رأى أهل الطائف اختلاف الشهب في السماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r5.speaker: عبد يا ليل بن عمرو
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r5.claim: Abd Ya'layl ibn Amr told them to check whether the stars remained in place; if so, heaven had not perished and the signs concerned Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r5.anchor: قال لهم عبد يا ليل بن عمرو : ويحكم أمسكوا عن أموالكم وانظروا إلى معالم النجوم , فإن رأيتموها مستقرة في أمكنتها لم يهلك أهل السماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r6.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r6.claim: In al-Suddi's version, the jinn told Iblis what happened; he sniffed earth brought from every region, identified Muhammad in Mecca, and sent jinn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r6.anchor: ففي رواية السدي أنهم أتوا إبليس فأخبروه بما كان من أمرهم , فقال : ائتوني من كل أرض بقبضة من تراب أشمها فأتوها فشمها فقال

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r7.claim: In Ibn Abbas's version, jinn searched east and west for the cause and found Muhammad reciting in Tihama.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r7.anchor: وفي رواية ابن عباس : أنهم رجعوا إلى قومهم فقالوا : ما حال بيننا وبين السماء إلا أمر حدث في الأرض , فاضربوا مشارق الأرض ومغاربها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r8.claim: The accounts differ over whether the Prophet saw the jinn: those who say they were directed to him say he saw, recited to, and summoned them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r8.anchor: ثم اختلفوا لاختلافهم في السبب , هل شاهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الجن أم لا ؟ فمن قال إنهم صرفوا إليه قال إنه رآهم وقرأ عليهم ودعاهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r9.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet said he had been ordered to recite the Quran to jinn and asked who would accompany him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p107/r9.anchor: روى ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( قد أمرت أن أتلو القرآن على الجن فمن يذهب معي ؟

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r1.claim: The continuation of Ibn Masud's report says the Prophet told him not to cross a line, then jinn descended like partridges and crowded around the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r1.anchor: قال : لا تجاوزه , ثم مضى إلى الحجون فانحدروا عليه أمثال الحجل حتى غشوة فلم أره

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r2.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r2.claim: Ikrima says the jinn at the encounter numbered twelve thousand and came from the island of Mosul.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة : وكانوا اثني عشر ألفا من جزيرة الموصل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r3.claim: Those who say the jinn searched across the earth to learn what had happened say the Prophet neither saw them nor recited to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r3.anchor: ومن قال إنهم صرفوا في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها لاستعلام ما حدث فيها , قال إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يرها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, says the Prophet did not see or recite to the jinn; they heard him praying dawn with companions at Nakhlah on the way to Ukaz.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r4.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال : ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علىالجن ولا رآهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r5.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r5.claim: Ikrima identifies the sūra the Prophet was reciting as al-Alaq.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r5.anchor: قال عكرمة : السورة التي كان يقرؤها { اقرأ باسم ربك }

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r6.speaker: زر بن حبيش
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r6.claim: Zirr ibn Hubaysh says there were nine jinn, including Zawba'a, who came to him at Batn Nakhlah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r6.anchor: فروى عاصم عن زر بن حبيش أنهم كانوا تسعة , أحدهم زوبعة , أتوه في بطن نخلة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r7.claim: Mujahid says seven came, three from Harran and four from Nasibin, and gives their names.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r7.anchor: وروى ابن جريج عن مجاهد : أنهم كانوا سبعة , ثلاثة من أهل حران , وأربعة من أهل نصيبين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says nine from a Yemeni village of Nasibin, distinct from the Iraqi one, heard him at dawn and prayed with him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r8.anchor: وحكى جويبر عن الضحاك أنهم كانوا تسعة من أهل نصيبين قرية باليمن غير التي بالعراق

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r9.claim: The account quotes the jinn returning to their people and urging them to answer God's messenger, echoing 46:29-31.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r9.anchor: فلما قضى ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين قالوا يا قومنا أجيبوا داعي الله وآمنوا به

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r12.claim: The jinn call the Quran amazing for its eloquence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r13.claim: The jinn call the Quran amazing for the eloquence of its exhortations.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r14.claim: The jinn call the Quran amazing for the greatness of its blessing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r15.claim: Rashd may mean right guidance in matters.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r16.claim: Rashd may mean knowledge of God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r17.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r17.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the Lord's jadd as His command.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Lord's jadd as His act.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r18.anchor: الثاني : فعل ربنا , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r19.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r19.claim: Mujahid glosses the Lord's jadd as His mention or remembrance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r19.anchor: الثالث : ذكر ربنا , وهو قول مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r20.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r20.claim: Ikrima glosses the Lord's jadd as His riches.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r21.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r21.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the Lord's jadd as His trial or favor.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r22.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r22.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses the Lord's jadd as His dominion and authority.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r22.anchor: السادس : ملك ربنا وسلطانه , قاله أبو عبيدة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r23.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r23.claim: Qatada glosses the Lord's jadd as His majesty and greatness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r23.anchor: السابع : جلال ربنا وعظمته , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r24.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r24.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the Lord's jadd as God's blessings upon creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r24.anchor: الثامن : نعم ربنا على خلقه , رواه الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r25.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r25.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads the phrase as meaning that God Himself is exalted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r25.anchor: التاسع : تعالى جد ربنا أي تعالى ربنا , قاله سعيد بن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r26.claim: A tenth possibility is that the jinn meant a grandfather, reflecting ignorance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r26.anchor: العاشر : أنهم عنوا بذلك الجد الذي هو أبو الأب , ويكون هذا من قول الجن عن [ جهالة ] .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r27.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r27.claim: Qatada says the jinn's fool means their ignorant, disobedient ones, as among human beings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r27.anchor: أحدهما : جاهلنا وهم العصاة منا , قال قتادة : عصاه سفيه الجن كما عصاه سفيه الإنس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r28.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r28.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify the fool as Iblis; a report from Abu Musa through his son also attributes this view to the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r28.anchor: الثاني : أنه إبليس , قاله مجاهد وقتادة ورواه أبو بردة بن أبي موسى الأشعري عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r29.speaker: أبو مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r29.claim: Abu Malik says shatatan means injustice; its root sense is remoteness from justice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r29.anchor: أحدهما : جورا , وهو قول أبي مالك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r30.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r30.claim: Al-Kalbi says shatatan means a lie, remote from truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r30.anchor: الثاني : كذبا , قاله الكلبي ، وأصل الشطط البعد , فعبر به عن الجور

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r31.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r31.claim: Another view says jinn know all human beings and therefore whisper to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r31.anchor: وقيل إن الجن تعرف الإنس كلها فلذلك توسوس إلى كلامهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r32.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r32.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says jinn descend from Iblis and humans from Adam; both peoples include believers and unbelievers and share reward and punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r32.anchor: عن الحسن البصري أن الجن ولد إبليس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r33.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r33.claim: On al-Hasan's account, believers from either people are God's allies, while unbelievers are devils.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r33.anchor: فمن كان من هؤلاء وهؤلاء مؤمنا فهو ولي الله , ومن كان من هؤلاء وهؤلاء كافرا فهو شيطان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r34.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r34.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r34.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas's view that jinn are children of al-Jann, not devils; they die and include believers and unbelievers, while devils descend from Iblis and live until his death.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r34.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس : أن الجن هم ولد الجان وليسوا شياطين وهم يموتون , ومنهم المؤمن والكافر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r35.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r35.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r35.claim: Those who say jinn descend from al-Jann rather than Iblis say they enter Paradise through faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r35.anchor: فمن زعم أنهم من الجان لا من ذرية إبليس قال يدخلون الجنة بإيمانهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r36.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r36.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r36.claim: If jinn descend from Iblis, al-Hasan says they enter Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r36.anchor: ومن قال هم من ذرية إبليس فلهم فيها قولان : أحدهما : يدخلونها وهو قول الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r37.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r37.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r37.claim: If jinn descend from Iblis, Mujahid says they do not enter Paradise, even if spared the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p108/r37.anchor: الثاني : وهو رواية مجاهد , لا يدخلونها وإن صرفوا عن النار .

MUJAHID:v2p697/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p697/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود
MUJAHID:v2p697/r1.claim: In a written reply to a question, Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd says the Prophet recited to the jinn at a ravine called al-Ḥajūn.
MUJAHID:v2p697/r1.anchor: كتبت إلى أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود أسئلة

MUQATIL:72:1/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:1/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:1/r1.claim: During the interval between Jesus and Muhammad, heaven was unguarded; after Muhammad's mission it was guarded and devils were pelted with meteors, prompting Iblis to investigate an earthly event.
MUQATIL:72:1/r1.anchor: وذلك أن السماء لم تكن تحرس في الفترة ما بين عيسى إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما بعث الله عز وجل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم حرست السماء

MUQATIL:72:1/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:1/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:1/r2.claim: Iblis sent the devils to find out what had happened, and they returned saying a prophet had been sent in Tihama.
MUQATIL:72:1/r2.anchor: فقال لهم إبليس: ائتوني بما حدث في الأرض من خبر، قالوا: نبى بعث في أرض تهامة.

MUQATIL:72:1/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:1/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:1/r3.claim: At the beginning of the mission, nine jinn from Yemen and the nobles of the jinn from Nasibin traveled to Tihama and reached Batn Nakhlah at night.
MUQATIL:72:1/r3.anchor: وكان في أول ما بعث تسعة نفر جاءوا من اليمن، ركب من الجن، ثم من أهل نصيبين من أشراف الجن وساداتهم

MUQATIL:72:1/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:1/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:1/r4.claim: The jinn found Muhammad praying the dawn prayer with companions and reciting Qur'an; they called it wondrous, meaning mighty and without equal.
MUQATIL:72:1/r4.anchor: فساروا حتى بلغوا بطن نخلة ليلا فوجدوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قائما يصلي مع نفر من أصحابه وهو يقرأ القرآن في صلاة الفجر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r1.claim: The command is for Muhammad to tell his community what was revealed to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ قل ﴾ يا محمد لأمتك ﴿ أوحي إلي أنه ﴾ أي الأمر والشأن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r2.claim: The majority open the hamza of “أنه” because it is the subject of “أوحي”; “أن لو استقاموا” and “أن المساجد” coordinate with “أنه استمع”, while “أن قد أبلغوا” follows the transitive verb “يعلم”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r2.anchor: أي الأمر والشأن أجمعوا على فتح أنه لأنه فاعل أوحى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r3.claim: The hamza is broken after a conditional fāʾ and after speech because the clause is an independent quotation.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r4.speaker: شامي وكوفي غير أبي بكر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r4.claim: Shami and Kufi readers other than Abu Bakr open the hamza in the clauses from “أنه تعالى جد ربنا” through “وأنا منا المسلمون”; others break it, connecting it to “إنا سمعنا” and pausing at verse ends.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في فتح الهمزة وكسرها من أنه تعالى جد ربنا إلى وأنا منا المسلمون ففتحها شامي وكوفي غير أبي بكر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r5.claim: A “نفر” is a group of between three and ten.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r7.claim: After hearing the Prophet recite during the dawn prayer, the jinn returned to their people and told them what they heard.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r7.anchor: لقومهم حين رجعوا اليهم من استماع قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة الفجر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r8.claim: They called the Qur'an wondrous and unprecedented in fine composition and sound meanings; “عجب” is a verbal noun used adjectivally.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p285#4/r8.anchor: عجيبا بديعا مبانينا لسائر الكتب في حسن نظمه وصحة معانيه والعجب ما يكون خارجا عن العادة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to tell his community that God revealed through Gabriel that a group of jinn listened; Ibn Abbas and others say he had not known before the revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r1.anchor: أي قل يا محمد لأمتك: أوحى الله إلي على لسان جبريل

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r2.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads aḥiya, preserving the original form; the source compares the change of wāw to hamza with 77:11.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «أحي» على الأصل يقال: أوحى إليه ووحى، فقلبت الواو همزة ومنه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r3.claim: Changing a wāw to hamza is generally permitted when the wāw bears ḍamma; al-Mazini extends the allowance to kasra and gives examples.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r3.anchor: وهو من القلب المطلق جوازه في كل واو مضمومة. وقد أطلقه المازني في المكسورة أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r4.claim: The apparent wording, especially istamaʿa, indicates that the Prophet did not see the jinn; the source links this to 46:29.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r4.anchor: فظاهر القرآن يدل على أنه لم يرهم لقوله تعالى: { استمع }

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet neither recited to the jinn nor saw them: a group at Nakhlah heard his dawn recitation and returned to warn their people.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r5.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم والترمذي عن ابن عباس قال: ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن وما رآهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the preceding report hasan sahih; it shows the Prophet did not see the jinn, though they attended and heard his recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r1.anchor: قال: هذا حديث حسن صحيح ففي هذا الحديث دليل على أنه عليه السلام لم ير الجن

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r2.claim: The jinn were with the devils when they searched for news because of the shooting stars; the ones pelted were jinn too.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r2.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الجن كانوا مع الشياطين حين تجسسوا الخبر بسبب الشياطين لما رموا بالشهب.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r3.claim: They were called devils because shaytan denotes anyone rebellious and disobedient; the Quran also speaks of human and jinn devils in 6:112.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r3.anchor: فإن الشيطان كل متمرد وخارج عن طاعة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r4.claim: A report graded hasan sahih says jinn used to ascend to hear revelation and add nine false words to each true word; after the Prophet's mission they were barred, informed Iblis, and found the Prophet praying near Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r4.anchor: كان الجن يصعدون إلى السماء يستمعون إلى الوحي فإذا سمعوا الكلمة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r5.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the pelted jinn told Iblis, who had them bring soil from their lands, smelled it, identified Mecca, and dispatched a group.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r5.anchor: وفي رواية السدي: أنهم لما رموا أتوا إبليس فأخبروه بما كان من أمرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r6.claim: One account says Iblis sent seven jinn, while another says nine, including Zawbaʿa.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r6.anchor: فبعث نفرا من الجن، قيل: كانوا سبعة. وقيل: تسعة منهم زوبعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r7.speaker: عاصم عن زر
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r7.claim: Asim from Zirr reports that Zawbaʿa and his companions came to the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r7.anchor: وروى عاصم عن زر قال: قدم رهط زوبعة وأصحابه على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r8.speaker: الثمالي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r8.claim: Al-Thumali says he heard that they were Banu al-Shaysaban, the most numerous and formidable jinn, who formed the main body of Iblis's troops.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r8.anchor: وقال الثمالي: بلغني أنهم من بني الشيصبان، وهم أكثر الجن عددا

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r9.speaker: عاصم عن زر
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r9.claim: Another report from Asim and Zirr says there were seven: three from Harran and four from Nasibin.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r9.anchor: وروي أيضا عاصم عن زر: أنهم كانوا سبعة نفر ثلاثة من أهل حران وأربعة من أهل نصيبين.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r10.speaker: جويبر عن الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r10.claim: Juwaybir reports from al-Dahhak that nine were from Nasibin, a town in Yemen distinct from the Iraqi town of that name.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r10.anchor: وحكي جويبر عن الضحاك: أنهم كانوا تسعة من أهل نصيبين قرية باليمن غير التي بالعراق.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r11.claim: Another account distinguishes the jinn who came to Mecca as from Nasibin and those who came to Nakhlah as from Nineveh.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن الجن الذين أتوا مكة جن نصيبين، والذين أتوه بنخلة جن نينوى.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r12.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r12.claim: Ikrima identifies the surah the Prophet was reciting as the opening of al-ʿAlaq, completed in the following passage.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3/r12.anchor: قال عكرمة: والسورة التي كان يقرؤها رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r1.claim: Ikrima says the Prophet was reciting Read in the name of your Lord (96:1); the jinn's names were already given in al-Ahqaf and need not be repeated.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r2.speaker: عامر الشعبي عن علقمة عن ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi asked Alqama about Ibn Masud's encounter with the jinn. Ibn Masud said he was not with the Prophet that night; later the Prophet told him a jinn caller had taken him to recite, showed him their traces and fires, and the jinn asked for food and fodder, which he supplied with a warning against using bones or dung for cleansing.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r2.anchor: روى عامر الشعبي قال: سألت علقمة هل كان ابن مسعود شهد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن؟

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Ibn Masud's account is more authoritative than Ibn Abbas's because Ibn Masud witnessed the event, whereas Ibn Abbas heard about it; eyewitnessing is not like report.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وابن مسعود أعرف من ابن عباس لأنه شاهده وابن عباس سمعه وليس الخبر كالمعاينة.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r4.claim: One reconciliation says the jinn came twice: first at Mecca in Ibn Masud's account, then at Nakhlah in Ibn Abbas's.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r4.anchor: وقد قيل: إن الجن أتوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دفعتين: إحداهما بمكة وهي التي ذكرها ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r5.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reconciles the reports by saying Ibn Abbas describes the first hearing, when the Prophet neither recited to nor saw them, and Ibn Masud describes a later summons when he recited to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r5.anchor: قال البيهقي: الذي حكاه عبد الله بن عباس إنما هو في أول ما سمعت الجن قراءة النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r6.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says sound hadiths show Ibn Masud was not with the Prophet on the night of the jinn, but went with him later to see their traces and fires; other routes place him there.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#2/r6.anchor: قال البيهقي: والأحاديث الصحاح تدل على أن ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r1.claim: In Ibn Masud's report, the Prophet asks who will accompany him to recite to the jinn; Ibn Masud volunteers, waits within a marked boundary, and is told they listened and returned as warners. They request provisions, receive bones and dung, and Muslims are forbidden to use them for cleansing.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r1.anchor: أمرت أن أتلوا القرآن على الجن فمن يذهب معي؟» فسكتوا، ثم قال الثانية

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r2.claim: Ikrima says the group numbered twelve thousand and came from the Island of Mosul.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة: وكانوا اثني عشر ألفا من جزيرة الموصل.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r3.claim: Another report describes jinn like men of Zutt with magpie-like faces; a tree came at the Prophet's call, testified to his prophethood, then returned to its place.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r3.anchor: فأتاه نفر منهم فقال أصحابنا كأنهم رجال الزط وكأن وجوههم المكاكي

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r4.claim: Another report says the Prophet rested his head on Ibn Masud's stone, awoke and asked for water to perform ablution; he used date water from Ibn Masud's vessel.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r4.anchor: أنه عليه السلام لما فرغ وضع رأسه على حجر ابن مسعود فرقد ثم استيقظ

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r5.claim: The source says the discussion of water and cleansing materials was already covered in al-Hijr and al-Tawbah.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r5.anchor: الثالثة قد مضى الكلام في الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says jinn descend from Iblis and humans from Adam; each kind includes believers and unbelievers, sharing in reward and punishment, with believers God's allies and unbelievers devils.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r6.anchor: فروى إسماعيل عن الحسن البصري: أن الجن ولد إبليس

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says jinn descend from al-Jann, not the devils; they include believers and unbelievers, while devils descend from Iblis and die only with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r7.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أن الجن هم ولد الجان وليسوا بشياطين

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r8.claim: Whether believing jinn enter Paradise depends on their origin: if from al-Jann, they enter through faith; if from Iblis, two views follow.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r8.anchor: واختلفوا في دخول مؤمني الجن الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r9.claim: If jinn descend from Iblis, al-Hasan's view is that believing jinn nevertheless enter Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r9.anchor: ومن قال: إنهم من ذرية إبليس فلهم فيه قولان

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r10.claim: Mujahid's reported view is that believing jinn descended from Iblis do not enter Paradise, though they are kept from Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#3/r10.anchor: الثاني وهو رواية مجاهد لا يدخلونها وإن صرفوا عن النار

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r1.claim: The source points to 55:56 as establishing that jinn enter Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r1.anchor: لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان [الرحمن: 56] بيان أنهم يدخلونها

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r2.claim: The jinn's request for provisions, especially bones, establishes that they eat and drink.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r3.claim: Some unbelieving physicians and philosophers deny jinn as simple substances unable to eat; the Quran and Sunna refute them, since no created being is simple and only God is truly one.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r3.anchor: وقد أنكر جماعة من كفرة الأطباء والفلاسفة الجن، وقالوا: إنهم بسائط، ولا يصح طعامهم اجتراء على الله وافتراء، والقرآن والسنة ترد عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r4.claim: No created being is simple: only God is truly one, while all other beings are composite.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r4.anchor: وليس في المخلوقات بسيط مركب مزدوج، إنما الواحد الواحد سبحانه، وغيره مركب وليس بواحد

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r5.claim: The Prophet could see jinn in their own forms just as he could see angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r5.anchor: وليس يمتنع أن يراهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صورهم كما يرى الملائكة.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r6.claim: Jinn most often appear to people as snakes.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r6.anchor: وأكثر ما يتصورون لنا في صور الحيات

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r7.speaker: الموطأ
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r7.claim: A report in al-Muwattaʾ tells of a recently married man who found a huge snake coiled on his bed and killed it with a spear.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r7.anchor: فإذا حية عظيمة منطوية على الفراش

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r8.claim: A sahih report says houses have resident jinn: warn a snake three times, then kill it if it remains; the Prophet called it an unbeliever and ordered its burial.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r8.anchor: وفي الصحيح أنه عليه السلام قال

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r9.claim: Some restrict the warning rule to Medina, citing a sahih report that jinn in Medina had accepted Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r9.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن ذلك مخصوص بالمدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r10.claim: The author rejects a Medina-only restriction: the report's rationale is the snakes' Islam, not Medina's sanctity, and that rationale applies elsewhere too.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r10.anchor: قلنا: هذا يدل على أن غيرها من البيوت مثلها لأنه لم يعلل بحرمة المدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#4/r11.claim: Reports that the encountered jinn were from the island and a general prohibition on killing house snakes support applying the rule beyond Medina.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r1.claim: One explanation of wondrous Quran is the eloquence of its language.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r1.anchor: { فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا } أي في فصاحة كلامه.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r2.claim: Another view finds its wonder in the eloquence of its exhortations.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r3.claim: Another view says it is wondrous for the greatness of its blessing.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r4.claim: Another explanation calls it mighty and without equal.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r4.anchor: وقيل: قرآنا عزيزا لا يوجد مثله.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r5.claim: Another explanation takes wondrous to mean great.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r12.claim: The jinn's discernment throws into relief the Quraysh polytheists' failure to recognize what reflection on the Quran showed the jinn.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r12.anchor: وفي هذا تعجيب المؤمنين بذهاب مشركي قريش عما أدركته الجن بتدبرها القرآن.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r13.claim: The unstated object of listened is the Prophet, supplied by the context; the jinn learned his recitation was God's speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r13.anchor: أي استمعوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعلموا أن ما يقرؤه كلام الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r14.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r14.claim: Al-Khalil defines nafar as a group of three to ten.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r14.anchor: والنفر الرهط قال الخليل: ما بين ثلاثة إلى عشرة.
